all.title: Intelligent Automation and Sustainable Performance of Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria: A Critical Review of the Roles of Operational Efficiency, Employee Adaptability and Organizational Agility
all.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
all.abstract: Intelligent automation is revolutionizing banking from digitization of consumer transactions to integration of robotic process automation, artificial intelligence, analytics, and connected workflows. Deposit money banks in Nigeria are making efforts in this regard to cut down costs, improve service quality, manage fraud, and cope up with competition from digitally minded financial service companies. But acquisition of technologies does not mean sustainable performance. This paper aims to critically assess how intelligent automation may affect the sustainable performance of deposit money banks in Nigeria in terms of finance, operations, people, and institutions. In this regard, this paper takes the form of a narrative and conceptual review where the focus is primarily on Nigerian literature but using international literature to draw theory and context comparison. The review finds out that there are three major interrelated explanatory mechanisms such as operational efficiency, adaptive capacity of employees, and organizational agility. With automation, banks can achieve faster, accurate, scalable, compliant, and supported decisions. On the other hand, these benefits can be hampered by incompatibility with legacy systems, lack of data, security risks, high cost of implementation, resistance from employees, skill mismatches, and poor governance. Using socio-technical systems theory, task-technology fit theory, resource-based view, dynamic capability theory, and human capital theory, this article presents a conceptual understanding of intelligent automation in the context of socio-technical organizational capabilities rather than being just a technology. This study pinpoints some conceptual ambiguity, short-sightedness about performance, weak indicators of automation maturity, and lack of longitudinal studies in Nigerian banking literature.

all.title: Predictive Analytics for Loan Approval and Comparative Bank Interest Rate Evaluation
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The loan approval process is a vital process within the Banking industry. A variety of factors are taken into consideration when approving a loan to an applicant. These include income, age, experience in employment, credit score, loan amount requested, education, property ownership, and previous loan history. Machine learning can be used to analyse the data and predict whether an application will be approved or denied. This research contains two parts. Part A contains a dataset with 45,000 entries of loan applications. This dataset includes a variety of information about the applicant including income, employment, credit score, loan amount, reason for loan, etc. The target column indicates whether the loan has been approved or denied. Various machine learning classification models such as Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) can be applied to the dataset. These can then be compared using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to see which machine learning model works best for predicting loan approvals. Part B of the research looks at comparing the lending rates of different banks using data provided by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The term loan rates for different banks can be compared. This can be simplified by looking at a set loan amount and time period. We can then calculate the estimated monthly EMI using the lending rates. This will help us understand how varying lending rates can impact the monthly repayment amount. This research combines machine learning to predict loan approvals and comparing lending rates. This can help us understand the key factors that relate to loan approvals and provides a simple way of determining which bank has the cheapest lending rates.

all.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Customer Behaviour Analysis and Predictive Marketing
all.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming marketing practices through advanced data analysis and predictive capabilities. This paper examines AI driven marketing, focusing on customer behavior analysis and predictive marketing. It explores how AI technologies help businesses understand customer preferences, identify purchasing patterns, and anticipate future customer actions. The study discusses applications such as customer segmentation, recommendation systems, sentiment analysis, customer churn prediction, and customer lifetime value estimation. It also examines AI applications across commerce, banking, healthcare, travel, hospitality, and social media marketing. The paper highlights potential benefits, including personalization, improved decision making, marketing efficiency, customer retention, and demand forecasting. However, effective implementation requires attention to data quality, privacy, algorithmic bias, implementation costs, and technical expertise. Ethical considerations, including transparency, consent, fairness, security, and human oversight, remain essential for responsible AI adoption. The paper follows a conceptual approach based on secondary literature. It concludes that AI can strengthen marketing effectiveness by integrating customer insights with predictive capabilities. Successful implementation requires collaboration between human marketers and AI technologies. This balanced approach can support customer relationships, informed decisions, and sustainable marketing performance.

all.title: A Design of an Effective Banking Application with Customer Churn Prediction and Enhanced Market Equilibrium Based Security Testing Through Machine Learning
all.venue: The International Journal of Maritime Engineering
all.abstract: Banking application and compliance with the EU PSD2 directive and the impact of protection motivation theory oninformation security. It identifies a gap in PMT literature and examines factors influencing consumer adoption of Fintech banking amidst ongoing digitalization. To overcome this issue, a new model has developed Customer Churn Prediction and Enhanced Market Equilibrium based Security Testing (CCMEST). This investigation proposes that integrating analytical modeling, market analysis, security validation, hypothesis testing, and machine learning will enhance banking applications through a model that factors in labor, capital, management, and effort using a Cobb-Douglas production function to assess firm value-added and managerial incentives and Cumulative distribution function (CDF). Companies will be evaluated on capital, management talent, and their effectiveness in achieving market equilibrium while assessing compensation and value-added. Security Testing involved 19 tests on banking API operations, focusing on secure communication, authentication, transaction fetching, and unauthorized request rejection. Hypothesis Testing evaluated statistical correlations using t-statistics, p-values, and PLS-SEM, with significant results determined by pre-set thresholds. Machine Learning Models applied UMAP for dimensionality reduction, followed by DBSCAN and K-means clustering, favoring K-means for its superior silhouette coefficient of 0.5225 compared to DBSCAN’s 0.5099. The performance analysis is CCMEST ML Model accuracy, precision, recall, F1-Score, CCMEST Overall Performance, CCMEST Overall Performance.

all.title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence in Commercial Transactions: Legal Challenges and Opportunities in Uganda
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is rapidly transforming commercial transactions by automating business processes, enhancing decision-making, facilitating digital payments, improving customer engagement, and enabling innovative contractual relationships. AI technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics, and automated decision-making systems are increasingly being adopted across sectors including banking, insurance, ecommerce, telecommunications, manufacturing, logistics, and financial technology. While these developments offer significant opportunities for improving efficiency, reducing transaction costs, increasing financial inclusion, and stimulating economic growth, they also present complex legal and regulatory challenges that existing commercial laws in Uganda are not fully equipped to address. Issues relating to contractual liability, algorithmic decision-making, consumer protection, data privacy, cybersecurity, intellectual property rights, competition law, electronic evidence, cross-border digital commerce, and accountability for autonomous AI systems continue to generate legal uncertainty and expose businesses and consumers to emerging risks. This study critically examines the regulation of Artificial Intelligence in commercial transactions in Uganda by evaluating the adequacy of the existing legal, institutional, and policy framework governing AI-driven commercial activities. It analyses the applicability of commercial laws, electronic transactions legislation, data protection laws, consumer protection principles, intellectual property regimes, and cybersecurity regulations in addressing legal issues arising from the deployment of AI technologies. The study further explores Uganda's preparedness to regulate AI in light of regional initiatives within the East African Community (EAC), continental developments under the African Union (AU), and international best practices, including the European Union AI regulatory framework and other comparative jurisdictions. Particular attention is given to

all.title: AI-Based Generative Structural Design for Reuse: Integrating Material Banks and LCA
institutions: Universidade Federal Rural do Rio de Janeiro
Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio de Janeiro
all.abstract: The transition of the construction industry towards a circular economy demands Structural Design for Reuse (StDfR) from end-of-life assets. However, designing with finite stock constraints imposes a complex combinatorial problem. Traditional approaches aiming for single optimal solutions limit diversity, presenting high computational costs and poor generalization. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a generative StDfR framework integrating Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), employing Reinforcement Learning and Graph Neural Networks parameterized by material banks. The model generated hundreds of diverse and viable structural designs in approximately five minutes, covering three truss topologies and various scenarios ranging from entirely new steel to full reuse. Notably, LCA revealed that full reuse does not guarantee the lowest environmental impact due to oversizing with reused elements, the transport of this additional weight, distances from deconstruction sites, and the reconditioning process, highlighting the efficiency of hybrid designs. By automating the information workflow between structural and sustainability teams, this AI approach provides agile StDfR support. Ultimately, the framework generates the final Building Information Modeling (BIM) model in the open Industry Foundation Classes (IFC), consolidating geometric, structural, and logistical project information. This tool empowers decision-making in conceptual phases, promoting the circularity of end-of-life assets.

all.title: **"Artificial Intelligence in Modern Horticulture: Enhancing Agrobiodiversity, Precision Farming, and Farmer Empowerment"**
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: --- ### Alternative Titles 1. **"Smart Farming for a Greener Future: The Transformative Role of AI in Horticultural Biodiversity and Precision Agriculture"** 2. **"From Seed to Market: How Artificial Intelligence is Revolutionizing Crop Management, Genetic Preservation, and Farmer Livelihoods"** 3. **"Digital Roots: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Horticulture to Optimize Yields and Empower Rural Communities"** 4. **"Beyond the Harvest: A Comprehensive Analysis of AI-Driven Precision Farming, Agrobiodiversity Conservation, and Inclusive Agricultural Growth"** 5. **"The AI-Horticulture Nexus: Leveraging Machine Learning and Data Analytics for Sustainable Crop Production and Farmer Welfare"** --- ### Subtitle**"A comprehensive analysis of how AI-driven technologies—including machine learning, computer vision, and predictive analytics—are transforming precision farming, preserving genetic diversity (as showcased by 400+ plant varieties), and empowering farmers for sustainable and profitable horticulture"** --- ### Detailed Description This research paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modern horticulture. Using the context of the All India Horticultural Fair in Telangana—which showcased over 400 plant varieties and significant female farmer participation (38% of 404 farmers)—the study explores how AI-driven technologies are addressing the critical challenges of climate change, resource scarcity, and sustainable food production. The paper is structured around four core analytical dimensions. **First**, it examines AI in precision horticulture and yield optimization. Computer vision algorithms applied through drones and cameras can detect plant diseases, pest infestations, and nutrient deficiencies at an early stage, enabling targeted interventions that reduce pesticide use. Predictive analytics models analyze historical weather and soil data to forecast yields, while AI-integrated smart sensors automate irrigation and fertigation systems to optimize water usage. **Second**, the paper investigates AI's role in agrobiodiversity and genetic resource management. The fair's exhibition of 180 varieties of *Gongura* (Roselle) serves as a case study for how AI algorithms can analyze vast genomic datasets to identify traits associated with drought tolerance, disease resistance, and higher nutritional value. The paper also discusses AI-driven crop variety recommendation platforms that match specific varieties to soil types and micro-climates, and AI-managed digital repositories for seed banks and herbariums. **Third**, the paper explores how AI empowers farmers through digital platforms. Natural Language Processing (NLP) enables AI chatbots to provide personalized farming advice in local languages via smartphones. AI-powered market intelligence analyzes trends to advise farmers on optimal selling times, optimizes supply chains to reduce post-harvest losses, and facilitates access to agricultural loans and insurance through alternative credit assessment models. **Fourth**, the paper addresses the challenges and future directions of AI adoption in horticulture, including the digital divide in rural areas, data privacy concerns, the prohibitive cost of AI-driven equipment for small-scale farmers, and the need for low-cost, user-friendly tools and public-private partnerships to ensure equitable access. The paper concludes that the intersection of AI and horticulture offers a promising pathway toward sustainable and profitable agriculture. By leveraging AI for precision farming, genetic resource management, and farmer advisory services, the horticultural sector can overcome modern challenges while preserving the agrobiodiversity championed by events like the All India Horticultural Fair. **Target readership:** Agricultural scientists, horticulturists, AI and data science researchers, agribusiness professionals, rural development policymakers, and graduate students in agriculture and technology. **Methodological note:** The paper is a conceptual and analytical review based on the themes presented in the source article. As the source article does not explicitly discuss AI, the paper extrapolates AI applications based on current literature and industry trends in precision agriculture and horticulture. --- *Would you like me to adjust the academic tone, shorten the description for a specific publication format, or generate a table of contents or abstract to accompany these elements?*

all.title: AI and Financial Sustainability in Banking- A Customer perspective
all.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is shaping the dynamics of doing business and has become a predominant change across domains and spheres. Banking is not an exception to this. AI in banking is now in its evolving stage and banks have started using AI in its day-to-day activities. AI has simplified routine repetitive tasks thereby increasing and improving the efficiency of doing banking business. This paper is an effort to arrive at an answer to the objectives: to understand customer knowledge and awareness regarding the adoption of AI tools in banks and to study the benefits and concerns of using AI in banking and also in promoting financial sustainability in banking. The scope of the study includes collecting responses from customers across Bengaluru, belonging to both public and private sector banks. The study data was collected from respondents using questionnaire circulated through google forms. Tables, Graphs, descriptive statistics and statistical tests are the tools used by the researchers s for the analysis. This study explores the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the banking sector, focusing on its role in enhancing efficiency and promoting financial sustainability. The study reveal that AI enhances customer service and convenience in comparison to traditional and manual service, not forgetting that it may affect the data privacy and cyber security.

all.title: Digital Immigrant Nomads and Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Challenges for Palestinian Academics – Structural Challenges as an Intermediary Factor
all.venue: International Journal of Applied Sciences & Development
all.abstract: The present study explores how the uptake of artificial intelligence (AI) tools relates to participation in digital freelance work among Palestinian academics who operate as digital nomads. Attention is directed to the ways these academics deploy AI applications across cross-border professional domains—research, teaching, and consulting among them—while confronting critical technical, financial, and political hurdles produced by geopolitical fragmentation. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design guided the investigation. Quantitative data came from an electronic survey completed by 150 academics affiliated with universities in the West Bank and Gaza Strip (N=150, a figure established through G*Power statistical analysis) and were processed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in Smart PLS 4, applying a bias-corrected bootstrapping procedure built on 5,000 resamples. To complete the empirical model, semi-structured interviews were held with 15 Palestinian academics, and the material was examined through thematic analysis until theoretical saturation had been reached. The results confirm that AI adoption produces a significant direct enhancement of digital academic work (β=0.420, 95% CI [0.312, 0.521], p

all.title: Analisis Komparatif Workforce Planning Berbasis Kapabilitas Pada Perbankan di Era AI
all.abstract: Perkembangan artificial intelligence (AI) mengubah karakter pekerjaan dan kebutuhan kapabilitas organisasi perbankan sehingga menantang perencanaan tenaga kerja yang bertumpu pada jumlah dan posisi. Penelitian ini menganalisis workforce planning berbasis kapabilitas pada perbankan Indonesia dengan membandingkan praktik yang terdokumentasi secara publik pada Bank Jago, BTN, dan bank bjb. Penelitian menggunakan analisis dokumen komparatif kualitatif atas 12 sumber publik yang dapat ditelusuri, dengan literatur ilmiah sebagai landasan konseptual. Melalui analisis isi kualitatif terarah, bukti dikodekan ke dalam empat dimensi, yaitu capability sensing, capability development, capability deployment, dan workforce readiness, serta diinterpretasikan melalui Human Capital Theory dengan literatur kapabilitas dinamis sebagai pendukung. Setiap bukti dinilai pada dua sumbu terpisah, yaitu keterkaitannya dengan AI dan kekuatan bukti praktik. Bank Jago memperlihatkan bukti yang relatif lebih jelas pada capability sensing; BTN lebih konkret pada reskilling dan penyesuaian peran; sedangkan bank bjb menekankan infrastruktur pembelajaran dan hambatan adopsi yang terdokumentasi. Bukti workforce readiness paling tipis pada ketiga kasus dan hasil pelatihan jarang terdokumentasi, sehingga perbedaan yang tampak dapat mencerminkan perbedaan pelaporan, bukan semata perbedaan praktik. Penelitian ini menawarkan kerangka analitis empat dimensi beserta tiga proposisi yang dapat diuji, dan menyarankan agar bank menghubungkan identifikasi kesenjangan keterampilan, pelatihan, dan penempatan serta mengukur hasilnya. Temuan bersifat interpretatif, bukan kausal, dan tidak dimaksudkan memeringkat bank.

all.title: KEY ASPECTS AND ADVANTAGES OF USING DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES IN FINANCE AND BANKING
all.abstract: In an era when the digital economy covers every activity, digital technologies already occupy a broad place in services, production and many other fields thanks to their convenience. This article treats as key elements the main functions that digital technologies perform in finance and the economy, as well as the functions and levels of usefulness of the digital applications in use within the system. Rapidly developing economic trends, together with the introduction and creation of new technologies across sectors, are making many industries more efficient. Various mobile applications are raising citizens’ financial literacy. Particular attention is paid to the broad use of modern technologies in financial transactions, to managing one’s accounts in financial and banking relations, and to improving online payments. In addition, the article covers online lending and automated credit scoring in the banking sector, the wide-scale advancement of FinTech technologies, the networked use of modern Big Data, and the extensive use of modern artificial intelligence in credit and financial assessments. Improvements in cloud technologies reduce network loads, while modern solutions such as Blockchain data and ERP systems, which are aimed at improving enterprise operations, together with the digitalization of financial reporting, are considered important for achieving the intended efficiency through the convenience and time savings they provide. The article may be useful for scientific and practical guidance.

all.title: Human Capital Development in Emerging Economies: Education, Skills Formation, and the Foundations of Long-Term Productivity
all.abstract: This report examines how the 93 middle-income economies holding 5.9 billion people, and the low-income countries behind them, can strengthen the human capital foundations of long-term productivity as digital infrastructure, automation, and artificial intelligence reshape labor demand. Built from public data on 172 countries covering 8.0 billion people (World Bank Human Capital Index and World Development Indicators) and situated within the H Heuristics Development Multiplier framework, it analyzes the learning crisis, early childhood foundations, secondary and TVET pathways, tertiary research, digital competencies, technology absorption, and ten sequenced priorities for 2026 to 2035.

all.title: Fintech, Financial Performance, and Financial Stability: A Hybrid Literature Review
all.abstract: The relationship between financial technology (FinTech), financial performance, and financial stability has become an increasingly important issue in banking and financial services. This review examines how digital banking, payment technologies, platform finance, artificial intelligence, big data, blockchain, and open banking influence profitability, operating efficiency, risk-taking, and resilience. Rather than assuming that technological adoption produces uniformly positive outcomes, the review focuses on the conditions under which FinTech creates financial value and the circumstances in which it introduces new vulnerabilities. The paper follows a hybrid review structure that combines a systematic search protocol with bibliographic mapping logic and qualitative content analysis. The literature is organised into three thematic clusters: (1) FinTech, bank performance, and competitive dynamics; (2) FinTech, bank risk-taking, and financial stability; and (3) digital innovation, financial inclusion, and the transformation of financial intermediation. Three cluster-based review tables summarise the research streams, representative studies, analytical approaches, theoretical foundations, and reported outcomes. The synthesis indicates that FinTech can improve efficiency, customer reach, innovation, and selected dimensions of bank stability. However, results are contingent on institutional context, bank characteristics, governance, technology integration, and regulatory capacity. Competition may compress incumbent margins, while cyber exposure, model risk, third-party concentration, and rapid digital funding movements can weaken resilience. The review contributes an integrated framework in which FinTech affects financial performance through efficiency, innovation, and information channels, while stability outcomes depend on risk governance, operational resilience, market structure, and regulatory oversight. The review offers implications for bank managers and regulators and identifies a future research agenda focused on causal identification, comparable FinTech measures, risk-adjusted performance, emerging markets, and systemic technology dependencies.

all.title: Digital transformation and economic development: Global and Chinese experiences
all.abstract: Overview: Digital transformation and economic developmentDigital transformation constitutes a system-wide reconfiguration of production, exchange and governance around general purpose digital technologies combined with organisational capabilities and public digital infrastructure that allow these technologies to scale up effectively across economic sectors (OECD 2024a(OECD , 2024b;; World Bank 2016).This reconfiguration operates through three interdependent architectural layers: infrastructure, applications and business models.The infrastructure layer encompasses high-speed connectivity networks, cloud computing and data centres, digital identity systems and instant payment platforms that provide the foundational computational and transactional capacity.The application layer comprises artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning algorithms, automation systems and advanced analytics tools that augment human cognitive capabilities and enable data-driven decision-making at scale.The business model layer is characterised by platform ecosystems and datadriven services that fundamentally restructure market organisation, value creation and competitive dynamics (OECD 2024a(OECD , 2024b)).Conceptually, digital transformation differs from previous waves of adoption of information technology (IT) in both scope and mechanism: rather than automating discrete tasks or processes, it reorganises entire production systems and governance structures through the scalable and non-rivalrous nature of digital goods and the network effects inherent in platform architectures (World Bank 2016).The empirical signature of this structural transformation is evident in sectoral composition shifts: in Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) economies, the information and communication technology (ICT) sector grew approximately three

all.title: Prediction of Credit Default Risk in Financial Institutions Using Artificial Neural Network
all.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTER SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY E-ISSN
all.abstract: This research study, examined the Prediction of Credit Default Risk in Financial Institutions using Artificial Neural Network. Credit default risk has remained one of the important fundamental and critical issues widely studied in the financial institutions in Nigeria. Credit Default risk comes into play when a loan borrower fails to repay his loan within the agreed financial contract. Banks and other financial institutions depend heavily on statistical and machine learning method in predicting loan default to the potential losses of granted loans. These machine learning applications cannot achieve full potential prediction without the semantic context in the data. Neural Network initiate the behavior of the human brain to solve both linear and non-linear statistical problems. The study observe that credit risk is the greatest and leading risk in the banking sector as its effects have crippled several financial institutions and have led to the failure of many. Therefore, the study proposed the adoption of Neural Network in predicting credit default risk to improve the prediction model’s accuracy and interoperability. Agile methodology, structured system analysis design methodology (SSADM) was used in the software development to get the total records of credit defaulters. This study designed a system for prediction of Credit Default Risk using Artificial Neural Network. The system is an efficient, accurate and reliable predictive tool which can be employed by financial institutions and lender organizations to solve and manage problem of credit default risk. The programming language PHP Script will be use for the software and My Structured Query Language (MySQL) for database.

all.title: The Impact of Digitalization and Technological Development on Tax Administration, Compliance, and Complexity: An Exploratory Study
all.abstract: The rapid pace of digitalization and technological development has fundamentally transformed modern tax systems. Advances in information and communications technology, artificial intelligence, and data analytics are reshaping the ways in which tax administrations operate, taxpayers comply, and governments design tax policies. Against this background, the paper has three specific objectives: to review the development and implementation of tax digitalization, to examine the impact of tax digitalization on tax compliance, and to assess the impact of tax digitalization on tax complexity. As part of the first objective, the paper considers, as a case study, the World Bank’s recently launched B-READY project, which highlights the growing importance of digitalization in the operation of tax systems worldwide. The paper draws on recent developments in Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, World Bank Group, and International Monetary Fund policy reports and the academic literature. The paper offers a conceptual framework for understanding the paradox of how digital transformation simultaneously promotes efficiency and transparency and reduces operational and computational compliance burdens on the one hand, while generating new forms of administrative and regulatory complexity on the other. The paper concludes by outlining key policy implications and suggesting directions for future research on balancing technological innovation with tax simplicity and equity.

all.title: TrustBound: Mechanized Completeness for Payment Epochs Initiated by AI Agents
all.abstract: Payment operations requested by an AI agent may remain executable, or their outcomes unresolved, after the agent has stopped. We study when a trusted payment service can account for every payment in an epoch and exclude further payments under earlier authority. We give a Lean model in which operations are recorded before they receive execution authority and both actions are serialized with an admission fence. We prove that fencing fixes a journal that covers every modeled effect and outstanding right; that discharging those rights prevents further effects; and that truthful outcomes for the recorded identities then give exact accounting. A provider-contract model, mapped to the admission model, makes created payment objects inert until registered. Premise-removal mutations confirm that each key premise is needed. We connect the models to an executable service: six service histories are checked against the model in Lean, and bounded schedules, scripted clients and concurrent workers exercise its reconciliation. The concurrent experiments uncovered a conflict caused by reordered provider reads, which serializing retrieval with journal updates removes in all tested cases. The result separates two obligations that are easily conflated in practice - preventing future payments and accounting for past ones - and states precisely which service guarantees establish each.

all.title: ATLAS-Finance: Benchmarking AI Agents in Realistic Banking Environments
all.abstract: Professional work involves under-specified assignments, where relevant information is spread across workplace applications and may conflict or change over time. To evaluate how well frontier agents can perform economically valuable work in such settings, we introduce ATLAS-Finance, a benchmark of 100 end-to-end investment-banking tasks across 13 simulated firms. As in real banking workflows, agents must search email, chat, calendars, notes, and files to identify requirements, gather information, reconcile conflicts/updates, and then build complex financial models. Tasks were developed by experienced bankers based on their real deal work and take them 15-30 hours to complete. Agent deliverables are evaluated with expert-authored rubrics (median: 124.5 criteria) covering financial rationale and results, spreadsheet construction, completeness, and formatting. Despite completing substantial portions of the requested work, current agents rarely produce correct deliverables. Across today's frontier models, the best ones (Claude Opus and Fable) pass fewer than 11% of tasks.

all.title: Agent Money Benchmark: Can AI Agents Be Trusted to Spend Money?
all.abstract: Giving an AI agent a wallet lets it buy data and services on a client's behalf. Trust then depends on how it spends money and what that spending achieves. We introduce Agent Money Benchmark (AMB) to test whether agents spend a client's money well, starting with purchases of information for financial decisions. We link seller quotes and payments to final answers, evaluating 12 models on 80 payment tasks with simulated sellers and 76 research questions using live data. Purchases settled in USDC on Solana mainnet via x402, a protocol for paying per web request. Three of the 12 models passed 79 of 80 payment tasks without payment or budget errors. Nine fell for a seller's trap at least once; repeat charges and above-list quotes accounted for 79% of scam events. We estimate waste from data and inference costs, counting failed payment tasks in full and research answers in proportion to missed points. With spending split equally between tracks, estimated waste ranged from \$21.0 per \$100 for Claude Fable 5.2 to \$70.8 for GPT-6 Luna.

all.title: Variable Zero: An Authority Gate for AI Agents Under Adaptive Attack
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: AI agents that act on a user's behalf can be steered by text hidden in the data they read. This technical report evaluates a deterministic authority gate (v0.3) that checks, in code, whether an agent's action has the user's authority before it runs. Rules were frozen before testing. On the AgentDojo banking suite, with three model families (GPT-6 Luna, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra) and adaptive attackers, including attackers told the gate's rules, no attacker action got through: the model was fooled and the gate was the last line of defense 561 times (95% upper bound on the failure rate about 0.5%). The report includes the gate's costs, false positives, two flaws found in the benchmark, a behavior we call self-answering, exploratory results on halt wording, and all limitations. Code and data are released.

all.title: Agentic AI Risk Management: Governance Protocols for Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems in Financial Services
all.abstract: The financial services sector is undergoing a fundamental transformation as institutions transition from reactive, prompt-based AI systems toward autonomous, goal-directed agentic architectures. Unlike prior AI deployments requiring structured inputs and continuous human oversight, agentic systems plan, reason, and execute complex multi-step workflows with minimal intervention. By 2026, adoption of agentic AI in financial operations is projected to exceed 600% growth, with global market spend approaching $50 billion and potential productivity gains of $3 trillion. This rapid deployment introduces a new class of systemic risks—including cascading failures, algorithmic collusion, adversarial prompt injection, and goal inversion—that existing governance frameworks are ill-equipped to address. This paper proposes the Agentic Trust Framework (ATF), a comprehensive governance architecture for monitoring, containing, and auditing autonomous agent workflows in financial institutions. The ATF integrates zero-trust identity management, blockchain-enhanced audit trails, semantic circuit breakers, and a tiered autonomy model grounded in formal control theory. We present Lyapunov-based stability guarantees for multi-agent containment, a priority-weighted resource conservation invariant, and GPTCTL trust operators for formal verification of agent behaviour. Real-world deployments at Itaú Unibanco, Visa, and Allianz validate the framework's applicability and effectiveness in high-stakes financial environments.

all.title: Governing Rogue AI Agents with Valid Credentials: A Reference Architecture for Business-Aware Autonomy Assurance in Agentic Enterprise Systems
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Technical white paper (v1.0, November 2026). Enterprise adoption of agentic AI is moving autonomous software from advisory roles into payments, ERP, supply chains, clinical systems and plant operations. Most agent security controls evaluate whether a single identity may perform a single action. This paper argues that the dominant failure mode of the next phase of enterprise AI is different: harmful business outcomes produced by agents that hold valid credentials and act within their permissions, either because they were manipulated or because several individually authorized agents compose into an outcome nobody approved. We define this class of failure as the rogue agent with valid credentials, introduce the concept of autonomy debt, and present a vendor-neutral reference architecture in which the model only proposes; an independent, deterministic action gateway decides; business-state invariants are enforced as policy-as-code (Cedar, OPA/Rego) in the systems of record such as SAP and other ERP; approvals are cryptographically bound to action fingerprints; limits are cumulative across agents; and a kill switch operates from a failure domain independent of the agent platform. The paper specifies a minimal control set, a six-rung agentic threat model (including the lethal trifecta and MCP tool-server supply chain), continuous-assurance signals, a new operational metric, mean time to provenance (MTTP), deployment guidance for SaaS, cloud, on-premises and edge, manufacturing and physical-AI controls with digital-twin rehearsal, a regulatory evidence mapping (SR 26-2, DORA, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001), an illustrative risk-economics model, a five-level maturity model and a 90-day implementation roadmap for CAIOs, CTOs, CIOs and CDOs. Companion article: The Rogue Agent Will Have Valid Credentials (also on DEV). About the author: Ganesh Raju is Chief AI & Innovation Officer (CAIO) and CTO at Elixir Global, Houston, Texas, with more than 15 years in AI, machine learning and data engineering. He is the founder and CEO of Akshaya.io and founder of RapidEVChargE (rapidevcharge.com); an investor, advisor and mentor; an open-source committer (Apache Bigtop, Hadoop, Spark, TensorFlow; former ODPi and Linux Foundation TSC); a participant in the Wharton Executive Education Chief Technology Officer program; author of AI Blockchain Design and Deployment; and former Vice Chair of IEEE Houston.

all.title: How Agentic AI Is Transforming Business Operations in 2026
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The way businesses operate is changing rapidly as artificial intelligence moves beyond answering questions and generating content. In 2027, organizations are expected to explore more autonomous systems that can understand objectives, make decisions, coordinate tasks and execute workflows with limited human intervention. This shift is making AI Consulting Services In Hyderabad increasingly relevant for businesses looking to adopt intelligent technologies and improve operational efficiency. One of the most important developments driving this change is Agentic AI, which has the potential to reshape how companies manage everyday operations, serve customers and make strategic decisions.What Is Agentic AI and Why Is It Becoming Important? Agentic AI refers to artificial intelligence systems designed to work toward specific goals by planning actions, using available tools, evaluating information and completing multiple steps with varying levels of independence. Unlike traditional automation, which generally follows predefined instructions, agent-based systems can respond to changing conditions and determine what actions may be needed to achieve an objective. For example, a conventional automation tool might send an invoice reminder according to a fixed schedule. An AI agent, on the other hand, could review payment records, identify overdue invoices, prepare personalized reminders, update the finance system and escalate unusual cases for human approval. According to the concept of an intelligent agent, an agent observes its environment and takes actions to achieve particular objectives. Agentic AI extends this idea through modern AI models, external tools, memory and planning capabilities. For business leaders, the importance of this technology is not simply about adopting another AI tool. It is about creating more connected, responsive and intelligent business operations. 1. Automating Complex Business Workflows One of the biggest opportunities for Agentic AI in 2027 will be the automation of complex business workflows. Many organizations still depend on employees to move information between departments, verify documents, update records and coordinate repetitive tasks. These activities consume valuable time that could otherwise be spent on strategic responsibilities. AI agents can help connect different stages of a workflow. For example, consider a purchase order process: - An AI agent receives a purchase request.- It checks the request against company policies.- It verifies available budget information.- It communicates with the appropriate systems.- It prepares an approval request for the responsible manager.- Once approved, it can help initiate the next steps in procurement. This approach can reduce manual coordination and improve the consistency of routine operations. Businesses can also explore workflow automation across human resources, finance, procurement, customer support and supply chain management. However, organizations should identify which processes are suitable for automation instead of attempting to automate every activity at once. 2. Transforming Customer Service and Customer Experience Customer expectations continue to increase. People want quick responses, relevant information and personalized assistance without unnecessary delays. Traditional chatbots are generally designed to answer specific questions or provide predefined responses. Agentic AI can potentially take customer interactions further by completing tasks across connected business systems. For example, when a customer reports a delayed order, an AI agent could: - Retrieve the customer's order details.- Check the latest delivery information.- Identify the reason for the delay.- Communicate an updated delivery estimate.- Create a support ticket if further investigation is required.- Notify the relevant team when human assistance is necessary. This can make customer support more responsive and reduce the workload associated with repetitive enquiries. Another opportunity is personalized customer engagement. AI agents can analyze available customer information and help businesses provide more relevant recommendations, follow-ups and support. Nevertheless, sensitive customer interactions, financial decisions and complaints involving unusual circumstances should have appropriate human oversight. 3. Improving Business Decision-Making Through Real-Time Insights Business decisions often depend on information collected from multiple departments, including sales, marketing, finance and operations. When this information is spread across different systems, managers may spend considerable time collecting and reviewing reports before making decisions. Agentic AI can help simplify this process by gathering relevant information, identifying patterns and presenting useful insights. Imagine a retail company experiencing an unexpected decline in sales. An AI-powered system could examine: - Recent sales performance.- Inventory availability.- Customer purchasing patterns.- Marketing campaign performance.- Regional demand variations. It could then prepare a report highlighting possible reasons for the decline and recommend areas that require further investigation. The final decision would remain with business leaders, but they could benefit from faster access to relevant information. Combining predictive analytics, machine learning and intelligent AI agents may also help organizations identify potential operational issues before they become larger problems. 4. Creating Smarter Finance and Accounting Operations Finance departments handle several repetitive but important responsibilities, including invoice processing, expense verification, financial reporting and payment follow-ups. Agentic AI could support these activities by coordinating information across accounting platforms and other business applications. For instance, an AI agent could review incoming invoices, extract relevant information, compare invoice details against purchase records and identify discrepancies. If everything matches predefined requirements, the system could prepare the invoice for approval. If it identifies unusual information, it could flag the issue for a finance professional. Other potential applications include: - Expense categorization.- Accounts payable assistance.- Payment follow-up coordination.- Financial document processing.- Budget monitoring.- Detection of unusual transaction patterns. These capabilities can improve operational visibility and help finance teams spend less time on repetitive administrative work. However, financial approvals and high-impact transactions should remain subject to appropriate authorization policies. 5. Transforming Human Resources and Workforce Management Human resources departments manage several processes that involve repeated communication, document verification and coordination. Agentic AI could help streamline these responsibilities while allowing HR professionals to concentrate on employee engagement, workforce planning and talent development. Some possible applications include candidate communication, interview scheduling, employee onboarding assistance, training recommendations and internal HR support. For example, when a new employee joins an organization, an AI agent could coordinate onboarding activities by preparing document checklists, sharing relevant information, scheduling introductory sessions and tracking completion status. It could also help employees find answers to common internal questions by retrieving information from approved company resources. However, recruitment decisions, employee evaluations and other sensitive workforce decisions require careful human involvement. AI systems should support these processes without replacing fair and accountable decision-making. 6. Enabling Collaboration Between Multiple AI Agents Another important development is the growing use of multi-agent AI systems. Instead of relying on a single AI agent to perform every activity, organizations can explore multiple specialized agents working together. For example, an enterprise marketing workflow could involve: - A research agent that gathers market information.- An analysis agent that identifies customer trends.- A content agent that prepares campaign material.- A reporting agent that organizes performance data.- A monitoring agent that identifies campaign issues. These agents can coordinate their activities through shared information and defined workflows. This approach may help organizations manage complex tasks more efficiently, particularly when different stages require different capabilities. However, multi-agent systems also introduce additional complexity. Businesses need to establish communication standards, access permissions, monitoring procedures and clear responsibilities for each agent. The objective should be to create coordinated systems that produce measurable business value rather than simply increasing the number of AI tools. 7. Strengthening Supply Chain and Inventory Management Supply chain operations depend on accurate information, timely coordination and the ability to respond to unexpected changes. Delays, inventory shortages, fluctuating demand and supplier-related issues can affect business performance. Agentic AI could help organizations monitor supply chain information and coordinate responses when operational conditions change. For example, an AI agent could monitor inventory levels, compare them against expected demand, identify potential shortages and prepare replenishment recommendations. If a supplier reports a delay, the system could examine alternative suppliers, compare available information and present possible solutions to the procurement team. Machine learning models can also support demand forecasting by identifying patterns in historical sales, seasonal trends and other relevant business information.
