all.title: Open Finance and Alternative Data for SME Credit Assessment in Underserved Markets
all.venue: Asian Journal of Economics Business and Accounting
all.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) frequently face credit constraints because collateral, audited accounts and formal borrowing histories provide incomplete or costly representations of their economic activity. Open banking, wider open-finance arrangements and alternative data promise to make transaction histories, payment flows, platform activity and administrative records usable in credit assessment. This critical narrative review evaluates when these information sources improve lending decisions, whether predictive gains translate into genuinely broader and more sustainable credit access, and which distributional and governance risks accompany data-intensive underwriting. Peer-reviewed empirical, theoretical and methodological literature published between 2006 and 24 August 2026 was examined, with earlier foundational work retained where necessary. The synthesis distinguishes evidence from small-business lending from consumer-credit extrapolations and separates improvements in model discrimination from causal effects on loan availability, pricing, repayment and enterprise performance. Recent studies from India, China, the United Kingdom and the United States provide credible evidence that verified payment and transaction information can complement traditional credit files, support new lending relationships and identify some previously underserved enterprises. Evidence is substantially less secure for informal, cash-intensive and digitally disconnected firms, and for benefits under economic stress. Greater data portability does not necessarily increase competition or welfare; access depends on consent, coverage, lender incentives and the market power of data intermediaries. Algorithmic models can reproduce exclusion through missing data, group proxies, selectively observed repayment outcomes and poorly calibrated adverse-action explanations. The review advances a conditional framework linking rights-based access, information quality, decision validity and enterprise outcomes. It argues that inclusive SME credit requires evaluation at the level of applicant participation and realised welfare rather than predictive accuracy alone. Research priorities include causal testing of data-sharing arrangements, stress-period validation, rigorous fairness audits and long-horizon measurement of enterprise resilience.

all.title: Impact of Open Finance Data Sharing on Credit Access for Unbanked and Underbanked Populations: A Systematic Review
all.abstract: In addition to being a great means of increasing financial literacy, open finance data sharing has proven itself to be a crucial instrument for enhancing financial inclusion through providing greater access to formal loans. This paper represents a systematic literature review based on a comprehensive analysis of 80 empirical articles written between 2009 and 2026 in different countries across five continents and related to the effects of open finance on the formal credit market. The analysis shows that open finance always positively impacts the probability of receiving loans but does not affect the extent of such an impact. If a country has developed credit bureau infrastructure, the probability of receiving formal loans increases by 3–9%, while in countries where people do not have any formal credit history, the probabilities usually go up by 15–30 percentage points or even higher. For instance, articles referring to the United States demonstrate the increase in the credit approval rate of 6–9 percentage points, and research concerning Peru indicates the increase from 16% to 31-48%. Besides, open finance makes loans more affordable due to a decrease in their interest rates in developed nations. Furthermore, thanks to sophisticated credit risk assessment algorithms, including psychometrics and artificial intelligence models, open finance allows increasing the credit approval rate by 13-30% while decreasing the default rate by 20-23%. The regulatory aspect should also be considered as strong privacy regulations and increased consumer autonomy contribute to better data sharing practices.

all.title: PRACTICAL ANALYSIS OF THE LEVEL OF ADOPTION OF OPEN BANKING AND API TECHNOLOGIES IN COMMERCIAL BANKS
all.venue: International journal of technology and academic research
all.abstract: This article presents an applied and empirical analysis of the adoption of Open Banking and Application Programming Interface (API) technologies in commercial banks. The study examines digital transformation in Uzbekistan’s banking sector, integration between banks and FinTech companies, and indicators of technological readiness using comparative analysis and a scoring-based assessment. The findings indicate that digital banks and neobanks demonstrate greater adaptability to Open API infrastructure, while monolithic IT architectures and the lack of unified national standards remain major barriers for large traditional banks. The article also presents a SWOT analysis of the Open Banking model and develops practical recommendations for introducing unified national API standards, strengthening cybersecurity, and improving consent management systems.

all.title: Embedded Finance in Restaurant POS Platforms: A Conceptual Framework for Saudi Arabia and MENA
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Restaurant point-of-sale (POS) platforms have become the system of record for small food and beverage (F&B) businesses. In Saudi Arabia, electronic payments reached 85% of retail payments in 2025, yet SME credit remained near 11.5% of total lending against a Vision 2030 target of 20%. This paper argues that the POS platform is a natural distribution and underwriting channel for SME finance, because it observes verifiable, high-frequency cash-flow and operational data that banks lack. We propose a four-layer conceptual framework for embedded finance in restaurant POS platforms: (1) payment acceptance and settlement, (2) the operational data layer, (3) embedded financial products, and (4) the partnership and regulatory layer. We link the framework to information asymmetry theory, two-sided platform theory, and recent evidence that cashless payments improve fintech lending outcomes. From it we derive six testable propositions on credit access, repayment, data value, delivery models, Shariah-compliant structuring, and platform lock-in. The paper contributes a context-specific model for Saudi Arabia and the wider MENA region, where open banking, buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) rules, and a rapid cashless transition create conditions for POS-embedded finance. It closes with implications for POS providers, licensed lenders, and regulators, and an agenda for empirical work.

all.title: O NOVO PETRÓLEO É DE SILÍCIO: ECONOMIA DE TROCA, ESCASSEZ DE GPUS E A DISPUTA GLOBAL PELO PODER COMPUTACIONAL
all.abstract: Este artigo discute as relações entre plataformas digitais, infraestrutura de semicondutores e dependência tecnológica, com atenção ao Brasil em perspectiva internacional. “Economia de troca” é empregada como delimitação operacional para examinar transações monetárias, tratamento de dados e acesso a serviços, sem equiparar economia compartilhada, plataformas e escambo. A abordagem é qualitativa e descritiva, com revisão narrativa e análise documental de textos acadêmicos, informações corporativas e instrumentos institucionais. A discussão distingue propriedade de hardware e contratação de processamento: restrições de oferta podem favorecer a contratação de serviços em determinadas condições, mas não demonstram uma transição inevitável ou irreversível. Dados da Nvidia ilustram a importância dos data centers na receita de uma empresa, sem representar todo o mercado de semicondutores. A comparação institucional identifica instrumentos industriais e regulatórios distintos nos Estados Unidos, União Europeia e Brasil, sem constituir uma tipologia exaustiva da China ou teste de políticas. Pix, Open Finance e os testes do Drex são tratados como iniciativas de naturezas e estágios diferentes, e não como sucessos equivalentes de infraestrutura. Conclui-se que a análise de soberania digital exige distinguir capacidades de projeto, fabricação, operação, regulação e segurança. Os materiais examinados não permitem mensurar causalmente os efeitos da escassez sobre concentração, trabalho ou dependência nacional.

all.title: Implementing central bank digital currencies in the countries of BRICS+: Problems and perspectives
institutions: National Research University Higher School of Economics
Moscow State Institute of International Relations
all.abstract: The article analyzes the issues of implementing national and cross-border projects of central bank digital currencies (CBDC) in the countries of BRICS+. CBDCs are considered as one of the main tools enabling wider use of national cur-rencies in international settlements and streamlining cross-border payments. This study focuses on 10 member countries of BRICS including five founding members (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa) and five new members that have joined the bloc during 2024—2025 (Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Indonesia, and United Arab Emirates), as well as Saudi Arabia that has not confirmed its membership yet, and 10 countries, which received the status of “partner countries” starting since January 1, 2025 (Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Vietnam, Uganda, and Uzbekistan). The CBDC projects were analyzed using the common approach that includes 14 parameters in three groups characterizing various aspects of national digital currencies’ systems as well as basic information on the financial sector development in the countries under consideration. The authors examined major features of research and development processes and realization of national and cross-border projects of digital currencies, identified main challenges and proposed measures aimed at resolution of critical issues to lay the foundation for systemic implementation of CBDCs in cross-border payments within BRICS+.

all.title: Regulating Central Bank digital currencies: financial stability, legal foundations and implications for Azerbaijan
all.abstract: The growing interest in central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) poses important questions about their legal nature, regulatory environment and implications for financial stability. This article examines the theoretical and legal underpinnings of CBDCs, noting their interactions with current monetary forms and possible impacts on the banking sector. The paper pays special attention to the risk of bank disintermediation arising from the shift of commercial bank deposits to CBDCs and to the regulatory responses intended to mitigate this risk. The article examines the key tenets of CBDC regulation proposed by the Bank for International Settlements and seven central banks, and argues that the recognition of public policy goals is a better principle than profit. In this context, the study examines the existing monetary legislation of Azerbaijan and determines the legal changes that need to be made to introduce a digital manat. Using the examples of The Bahamas and China, it proposes a regulatory framework for the issuance and legal tender status of the digital manat, ensuring user privacy, compliance with anti-money laundering rules, and financial stability. The article states that a successful launch of a CBDC in Azerbaijan needs a solid legislative framework and regulatory safeguards that are specifically tailored to fit the unique features of the country's financial system. Keywords: CBDC, money flower, financial stability, central bank, AML/CFT, IMF, Sand Dollar, e-CNY, digital manat.

all.title: Central Bank Digital Currency as a Circular Economy Facilitator: A Study of Law, Finance, and Governance in the Transition
all.abstract: The global shift toward a circular economy (CE) is essential to counter resource depletion and environmental degradation, while the emergence of Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) offers a parallel opportunity to enhance transparency and accountability in economic transactions. This chapter examines the legal, financial, and governance dimensions of CBDCs as strategic facilitators of CE integration, using an interdisciplinary approach spanning economics, finance, law, and public policy. It develops a conceptual framework linking CBDC implementation to circular economy outcomes through financial inclusion, digital innovation, and stakeholder coordination, exploring how programmable currencies can optimize resources, enable green finance, ensure supply chain traceability, and strengthen public-private cooperation. Structured across three sections covering theoretical linkages, regulatory frameworks, and policy pathways, the chapter concludes that CBDCs can accelerate a data-driven, inclusive, and sustainable circular economy.

all.title: CENTRAL BANK DIGITAL CURRENCIES (CBDCS) AND CROSS-BORDER PAYMENT EFFICIENCY IN EMERGING MARKETS: A DYNAMIC STOCHASTIC GENERAL EQUILIBRIUM (DSGE) APPROACH NIGERIA CASE STUDY (2010–2024)
all.abstract: This study examines the impact of Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) adoption on cross-border payment efficiency in Nigeria using a Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) framework. The eNaira, launched by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) in October 2021, represents Africa's first retail CBDC. Using quarterly data from 2010:Q1 to 2024:Q4, we estimate a medium-scale DSGE model incorporating financial frictions, cross-border payment costs, and CBDC adoption dynamics. The Bayesian estimation results indicate that CBDC adoption shocks significantly improve cross-border payment efficiency, reduce exchange rate volatility, and enhance remittance inflows. Impulse response functions reveal that a one-standard-deviation CBDC adoption shock increases cross-border payment efficiency by 1.2% in the short run and 0.8% in the long run. Variance decomposition analysis shows that CBDC shocks explain approximately 18% of the forecast error variance in payment efficiency at the 20-quarter horizon. The findings provide strong evidence for the welfare-enhancing potential of CBDCs in emerging market economies and offer policy recommendations for optimizing digital currency frameworks in Sub-Saharan Africa.

all.title: Algorithmic Foundations of Digital Currency Systems:A Critical Survey of Central Bank Digital Currencies and Cryptocurrencies
all.abstract: Digital currencies represent a fundamental structural shift in the modern financial system, raising critical questions regarding monetary sovereignty, algorithmic trust, and user privacy. Although existing literature frequently addresses the challenges of stability, governance, scalability, and adoption surrounding cryptocurrencies and Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs), these dimensions are largely examined in isolation. This critical review adopts an information technology perspective to evaluate whether current scholarship provides a unified, practical taxonomy of digital currency architectures. Drawing on a structured critical review of 30 purposively selected peer-reviewed studies and institutional reports, the study evaluates cryptographic foundations, validation schemes, ledger structures, privacy frameworks, and performance attributes, the study evaluates cryptographic underpinnings, validation schemes, ledger structures, privacy frameworks, and performance attributes. The findings reveal a prominent research gap: no current framework simultaneously reconciles sovereignty, privacy, security, and scalability. This limitation underscores the emergence of hybrid algorithmic designs as an essential architectural direction for future digital currency systems.

all.title: Blockchain Innovation and Central Bank Digital Currency Readiness Among Financial Technology Firms in Nairobi County, Kenya
all.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital financial technologies has intensified global interest in Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) as a potential instrument for improving payment systems, financial inclusion and transaction security. However, the extent to which fintech firms are organizationally and technologically prepared to support a potential retail CBDC remains insufficiently established. This study examined the influence of blockchain innovation on CBDC readiness among financial technology firms in Nairobi County, Kenya. Specifically, the study examined the influence of blockchain-enabled process innovation and blockchain-enabled service innovation on CBDC readiness. The study was anchored on Systems Theory, Modern Portfolio Theory, Transaction Cost Theory, and Public Interest Theory of Regulation. An explanatory research design was adopted, targeting 144 licensed fintech firms in Nairobi County, from which 113 responses were obtained. Primary data were collected using structured questionnaires administered to relevant senior management personnel, and the data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis and multiple regression analysis. The regression results showed that the four blockchain innovation dimensions jointly accounted for 83.6% of the variation in CBDC readiness (Adjusted R² = .836), and the overall regression model was statistically significant, (F (2,109) =290.039, p<0.001). Individually, blockchain process innovation and service innovation were statistically significant predictors of CBDC readiness based on the reported regression results. The study concludes that blockchain innovation is significantly associated with the readiness of fintech firms to operate within a potential CBDC environment. The study recommends continued development of enabling policies for interoperability, investment in blockchain-enabled process and service innovation, and strengthening of security, transparency and internal controls among fintech firms. Key terms: blockchain innovation, process innovation, service innovation, CBDC readiness, fintech firms in Kenya

all.title: Central Bank Digital Currency, Deposit Substitution and Bank Net Interest Margins - A Theoretical Scenario Analysis with Monetary Policy Sensitivity
all.abstract: This paper examines how the monetary policy environment conditions the banking cost of retail central bank digital currency (CBDC). Using a theory-driven, no-sampling, scenario-based analytical framework, we evaluate four stylized CBDC policy configurations across three monetary policy rate environments representing low-rate, baseline, and elevated funding cost conditions. The central finding is that the net interest margin compression caused by CBDC-induced deposit substitution is not determined by CBDC design alone. It depends materially on the cost of alternative bank funding, and this dependence is amplified by the quantity of CBDC in circulation. The interaction is multiplicative, permissive CBDC design and elevated funding costs are complements in generating margin pressure, not independent risks. This implies that optimal CBDC holding limits are not rateenvironment-neutral, and that design rules calibrated under low-rate conditions may be systematically too permissive during monetary policy tightening cycles. JEL codes: E42, E58, G21, G28, E52, O33

all.title: CBDC remuneration and the limits of neutrality under CES preferences
institutions: Central University of Finance and Economics
all.abstract: We examine whether wealth-neutral central bank digital currency (CBDC) remuneration preserves real allocations under constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) preferences. Wealth neutrality denotes unchanged total real liquid balances, whereas allocation neutrality requires unchanged real activity. Extending the log-separable benchmark, we derive an implicit remuneration condition and an exact decomposition into general interest rate, non-separability and intratemporal-elasticity channels. At a CBDC-to-GDP ratio of approximately 14%, the calibrated wealth-neutral equilibrium raises output by 0.027% and consumption by 0.031%. The contribution is primarily conceptual: exact allocation neutrality depends on preference and equilibrium restrictions, while the departures are quantitatively modest in this calibration. The exercise does not identify an optimal CBDC rate or establish large welfare effects.

all.title: Strengthen the signal, weaken the system? CBDC design trade-offs and monetary implications
all.venue: Journal of Banking and Financial Technology

all.title: CBDC competition between China and the European Union: A political steering theory perspective
all.abstract: The introduction of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) has become intertwined with geopolitical and geoeconomic competition over payment infrastructures, payment standards, and monetary sovereignty. This article examines the developments of China’s e-CNY and the European Union’s (EU’s) digital euro within the context of an emerging digital monetary order, exploring them as interdependent steering sequences. By introducing political steering theory (PST) as an interaction-oriented approach to foreign policy analysis, we explore how actors’ problem perceptions translate into largely indirect (and at times meta-)steering attempts, and how these attempts trigger counter-steering. Through qualitative document analysis and process tracing, this article reveals that China has sought to re-embed domestic payment infrastructures, while also attempting to shape cross-border settlement conditions and standard-setting processes. In response, the EU and the European Central Bank have primarily employed indirect counter-steering, notably by advancing the digital euro, tightening regulatory conditions for digital currencies within their jurisdiction, and engaging in coalition building and interoperability efforts. This analysis demonstrates the value of PST in explaining CBDC-related foreign-policy processes as sequences of (counter-)steering driven by problem perceptions and solution seeking in digital finance.

all.title: CBDC Issuance and the Legal Challenges of Safeguarding Central Bank Independence
all.abstract: 중앙은행 디지털화폐(CBDC)의 도입은 결제수단을 디지털화하는 문제를 넘어, 중앙은행 독립성의 법적 기반 전반을 다시 설계할 것을 요구하는 규범적 과제를 제기한다. 본 연구는 한국은행법상 중앙은행 독립성의 법적 근거를 확인하고, CBDC 도입이 발권독점과 통화주권, 통화정책 수행의 독립성, 재정정책과의 경계, 데이터 거버넌스와 감시권력이라는 네 차원에서 독립성을 어떻게 위협하는지를 법리적으로 분석한다. 비교법적으로는 EU(TFEU 제130조와 디지털 유로 규정안), 미국(GENIUS Act와 연방준비법 제16A조), 중국(e-CNY), 영국(디지털 파운드 컨설테이션)이 택한 규범 체계와 정책 선택을 한국의 프로젝트 한강과 대비하여, 독립성의 법적 보장 방식과 CBDC 규율 방식 사이에 일정한 유형적 연관성이 있음을 확인한다. 이러한 분석을 바탕으로 본 연구는 CBDC 시대의 중앙은행 독립성을 보장하기 위한 다섯 가지 법제 설계 원칙, 곧 발행 권한의 법률적 명문화, 통화정책 수단 독점성 보호 조항의 신설, G2P 재정집행 참여의 목적 법정주의, 데이터 거버넌스 독립 감독체계의 구축, 스테이블코인과의 법적 위계의 선제적 확립을 제시한다.

all.title: Same Euro, Different Tax? The Digital Euro, Bank-Issued E-Money Tokens and Tokenized Deposits under EU Tax Law
all.abstract: The emergence of the digital euro, euro-denominated e-money tokens and tokenized commercial bank deposits is creating three technologically similar, but legally distinct, forms of digital money in the European Union. While financial regulation differentiates these instruments according to issuer, redemption rights and underlying claim, EU and Member State tax rules remain fragmented and technology-neutral only in theory. This article examines whether conversions, payments, remuneration and cross-border holdings involving these instruments may produce different direct tax, VAT and tax reporting consequences despite their shared monetary function. Particular attention is paid to the interaction between MiCA, the proposed digital euro framework, DAC8, the amended Common Reporting Standard and recent CJEU case law. The article argues for a principle of monetary-functional tax neutrality: economically equivalent euro-denominated digital money should receive equivalent treatment, while genuine yield, investment risk and intermediary services should remain taxable according to their substantive characteristics.

all.title: What Does the Rise of Digital Currencies (CBDCS) Mean for Monetary Sovereignty in the Global South?
all.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
institutions: United World College of South East Asia
all.abstract: The pace of CBDC developments brought about a new discourse on the future of monetary system architecture and money state sovereignty in particular, especially in emerging countries. Using a qualitative literature review supported by available data and comparative case studies, this paper examines the implications of CBDCs for monetary sovereignty in the global south. It explains the rationales of CBDC introduction, including financial inclusion, modernization of the payments system, competition with digital private money and geopolitical considerations. In addition, this paper reviews the potential of CBDCs in terms of the implications of monetary policy, financial stability, fiscal capability, and payments autonomy. Comparative analysis of CBDC results in India, Nigeria, Bahamas and Brazil (etc.) demonstrates that the impact of CBDCs might differ from one country to another depending on the quality of institutions and governance, as well as digital infrastructure. It becomes clear that the CBDCs are not only innovations in digital technologies, but also policy instruments at the same time. However, their potential to strengthen monetary sovereignty is based not only on digital technologies, but also on proper legal framework, efficient institutions, inclusive introduction, and trust of the population.

all.title: Beyond the 99% Recovery: How Programmable CBDCs Can Break the Climate-Debt Trap in Bangladesh
Weaponized Interdependence, Payment Systems, and Distributed Ledger Technologies: Examining Policy Challenges and Opportunities in Financial Infrastructure
all.venue: Springer studies in law & geoeconomics/Springer studies in law & geoeconomicsd

all.title: The digital money trilemma
all.abstract: Central banks worldwide are primarily exploring central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) to meet domestic goals such as improving monetary policy transmission, advancing digitalisation, and promoting financial inclusion. However, growing interest in cross-border applications has raised geopolitical and economic concerns, particularly for developing countries given their greater exposure to spillovers from CBDC adoption in advanced economies. This chapter examines the international political economy of cross-border CBDC design from the perspective of emerging market economies. It frames these challenges through a “Digital Money Trilemma”, highlighting the trade-off between leveraging digitalisation for sustainable development, such as more efficient remittance flows, while simultaneously safeguarding against currency substitution and policy lock-in. This chapter argues that domestic policy and technical design choices alone are insufficient to counter existing structural power asymmetries. For cross-border CBDCs to effectively support inclusive and sustainable development, technical interoperability must be matched by equitable international governance and meaningful North–South cooperation.

all.title: Navigating the path to deeper financial inclusion
all.abstract: The Central Bank of Indonesia (BI) issued a White Paper on the Digital Rupiah, Indonesia’s Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), in 2022, in which one of the objectives is to deepen financial inclusion. Using a qualitative analysis approach that combines in-depth interview and descriptive analysis on the level of Indonesian digital economy and socio-economic conditions, this research found that the proposed design of the Indonesian CBDC might not effectively achieve BI’s objectives to deepen financial inclusion. Indonesia already has a well-developed digital payment ecosystem and mature e-payment industries, both of which have played a significant role in bridging financial inclusion gaps in Indonesia. Yet, the challenge of deepening inclusion extends far beyond service digitalisation, as it is fundamentally rooted in the country’s structural and socio-economic conditions. The need to emphasise in addressing structural issues such as economic inequality, digital divide, national ID, and digital and financial literacy is a key factor in deepening financial inclusion. CBDCs can contribute to this process by leveraging the granular data generated through CBDC usage to transform socio-economic programmes and by utilising CBDCs for cross-border transactions. In turn, deeper financial inclusion in Indonesia can be achieved, which would also support the sustainable development agenda.

all.title: Overview of the Unique Regional Applications, Risks, and Regulatory Challenges of China's Digital RMB
all.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
all.abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid global advancement of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), China, as the world's most populous developing economy, has pursued a distinctive development trajectory for its digital fiat currency, the e-CNY. Adopting a literature review and comparative analysis approach, this paper systematically introduces the two-tier operating system of e-CNY, its domestic pilot programs, and cross-border trial initiatives. It also compares e-CNY with retail CBDCs deployed in both developing and developed economies. The study finds that e-CNY demonstrates clear strengths in advancing financial inclusion, improving payment efficiency, and enhancing the precision of monetary policy transmission. However, it also faces notable risks, including privacy protection concerns, potential disintermediation of commercial banks, and technical security vulnerabilities in offline payment scenarios. This paper further discusses targeted regulatory solutions, including tiered anonymity rules, conversion limits, and central bank liquidity support mechanisms. This research deepens understanding of the opportunities and risks associated with large-scale retail CBDC deployment, and offers references for China and other economies to refine digital currency regulatory frameworks.

all.title: Assessing the Feasibility of De-Dollarisation and the Quest for Alternatives
all.abstract: Since the Bretton Woods agreement, the US dollar has dominated international trade and finance as the primary medium of exchange, store of value, and unit of account. This hegemony has conferred significant advantages upon the United States, including the so-called ‘exorbitant privilege’. However, recent years have witnessed growing concerns over the sustainability of a dollar-centric system, prompted by the US government's expansionary fiscal and monetary policies, recurrent debt ceiling crises, and the increasing use of the dollar as a geopolitical tool. These developments have eroded confidence in the dollar's stability, prompting central banks to diversify their reserves into alternative currencies and gold. The BRICS+ countries, which now account for a larger share of global GDP than the G7, have expressed strong interest in reducing their reliance on the dollar, exploring regional payment systems, and the potential for a common currency. Despite these efforts, the dollar's dominance persists, underpinned by network externalities, established financial infrastructure, and the absence of viable alternatives. Technological innovations, such as central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and blockchain-based platforms, may eventually facilitate de-dollarisation by lowering transaction costs and enabling new forms of cross-border settlement. However, the transition away from the dollar in international finance is likely to be slow and fraught with challenges, as no single currency currently offers the liquidity and stability required to replace the dollar. This chapter evaluates the mechanisms and implications of de-dollarisation, highlighting both the opportunities and obstacles in moving towards a more multipolar international monetary system

all.title: Willingness to Use and Actual Use of e-CNY: Mediation Mechanisms Within a Mature Payment Ecosystem
all.abstract: The e-CNY pilot programs have expanded steadily in recent years, reflecting China’s continued efforts to promote its central bank digital currency (CBDC). However, actual use of the e-CNY remains low in China’s mature payment ecosystem. This study examines the antecedents of willingness to use and actual use of the e-CNY and their mediation pathways by extending the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) with trust, perceived risk, and innovation resistance. Data were collected from 509 respondents and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and explainable machine learning. PLS-SEM was employed to examine the effects of the antecedents on willingness to use and actual use and to identify their mediation types. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to assess their relative predictive importance. The results reveal that social influence, trust, and innovation resistance are the key factors associated with willingness to use, whereas performance expectancy and effort expectancy are not significant. When actual use is measured by self-reported transaction items only, the three significant factors are associated with actual use only through willingness to use. The mediation types differ, however, under the full five-item measure, which also covers recommendation and future use plans: social influence and innovation resistance exhibit complementary and indirect-only mediation, respectively, while trust shows a competitive mediation. The total effect of trust is not significant under either measure. These findings suggest that efforts to promote e-CNY adoption in China should address social influence, trust, and innovation resistance in addition to performance expectancy and effort expectancy, offering practical guidance for wider adoption and potential implications for the sustained use of digital public payment infrastructure.

all.title: SMART BANKING SYSTEM (GREEN BANKING) A UNIFIED, SECURE AND INTELLIGENT CORE BANKING PLATFORM FOR CUSTOMERS, COMPLIANCE OFFICERS, AND ADMINISTRATORS
all.abstract: Modern financial operations and digital banking exist in a mission-critical area where security vulnerabilities, unauthorized overdrafts, fraudulent transactions, money laundering risks, and manual credit underwriting delays can profoundly undermine institutional integrity and customer trust. This paper proposes Green Banking (Smart Banking System), a unified, secure, and intelligent core banking platform connecting retail customers, compliance officers and bank administrators through a real-time digital financial ecosystem. The system is focused around an atomic double-entry General Ledger bookkeeping engine, two-step OTP multi-factor authentication, real-time AI Neural Sentinel fraud and anomaly detection, automated Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance monitoring, CIBIL-based loan underwriting with reducing-balance EMI amortization schedules, ISO/IEC 7812 Luhn Mod-10 card lifecycle management and standardized identifier generation (IFSC, UPI VPA and ISO 13616 IBAN). The platform is built using a four-tier architecture encompassing a presentation tier, an Express REST API gateway tier, a business services tier and an ACID-compliant persistence tier utilizing SQLite in Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) mode. Security is enforced through JWT-based Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), bcrypt password hashing and tamper-evident audit logging and the API is documented with OpenAPI/Swagger. The primary aim of the system is to transform every banking operation into an atomic, verified and auditable lifecycle in which no transaction is committed without balance verification, AML screening and fraud-risk scoring. The proposed design also serves as the foundation for future technologies including blockchain-based ESG bond tokenization, IoT smart-meter verification, Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) settlement and biometric authentication.

all.title: Impact of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and Digital Payments on India's Economic Growth: Macroeconomic Channels, Financial Inclusion, and Structural Formalization
all.abstract: The rapid proliferation of digital payment architectures, anchored by the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), has triggered a structural paradigm shift in the Indian economy. Evolving over a decade from its launch in 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) into the world's largest real-time retail payment mechanism, UPI now processes nearly half of the globe's real-time digital transaction volume, crossing 241 billion annual transactions with an aggregate turnover exceeding ₹314 lakh crore (~US$ 3.8 trillion) in FY 2025-26. This paper investigates the empirical and theoretical transmission channels through which UPI and retail digital payments propel India's macroeconomic expansion and structural modernization. Grounded in monetary economics (velocity of money formulation), Transaction Cost Economics, and Financial Intermediation Theory, this study analyzes how digital payment public infrastructure (DPI) accelerates gross domestic product (GDP) growth. Specifically, the paper delineates four primary macroeconomic transmission mechanisms: (1) drastic reductions in transaction friction and cash-handling logistical costs, which historically consumed 1.5% to 2% of GDP; (2) structural formalization of the informal sector and unprecedented expansion of fiscal tax buoyancy (evidenced by record GST revenues); (3) democratization of micro-credit through the digital financial footprint of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) leveraging Credit-on-UPI and the Account Aggregator framework; and (4) friction-free public welfare distribution via Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT) under the Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity. Concurrently, the paper critically interrogates emergent systemic vulnerabilities: the zero-Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) sustainability dilemma, fintech duopolistic market concentration, escalating cyber-fraud vectors, and digital exclusion in marginalized regional cohorts. Finally, the study outlines strategic policy interventions to preserve infrastructural resilience, bolster digital literacy, integrate Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDC e-Rupee), and expand UPI's cross-border geoeconomic footprint.

all.title: Clean-Account Banking, Zero Hidden Money, and Multi-Tier Protection Against Corrupt Agencies: Reclaiming Cryptographic Ledgers From Speculative Coin Schemas
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Eliminating Illicit Money Laundering, Proof-of-Work Speculative Waste, and Unchecked Institutional Snooping Through Provenance-Closed Double-Entry OMVFS01 Ledgers, Four Graduated Secret Tiers, and Adversarial Threshold Quorum Warrants (OMVFS-BANK-V1) Cryptographic hash chains and Merkle trees were invented for a noble, natural purpose: tamper-evident accounting, double-spend prevention, and mathematical auditability. Speculative cryptocurrency schemas hijacked that breakthrough — attaching Proof-of-Work coin mining and anonymous token casinos that burn nation-scale electricity while serving ransomware cartels, wash traders, and dirty-account money laundering. Yet the state-surveillance alternative — centralized Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) or unchecked agency databases — hands a single ministry god-mode visibility over every citizen's life, turning into an extortion weapon whenever an agency or official becomes corrupt. OMVFS-BANK-V1 solves both sides simultaneously: clean accounts form a mathematically closed Kirchhoff conservation graph where unattributed dark-silo money cannot enter (binding ordinary citizens, corporations, and public officials under the exact same math), while honest people are shielded by four graduated OMVFS secret-protection tiers, (t, n) adversarial multi-institution quorum warrants, single-field Merkle openings, and unforgeable reverse-audit scars that expose any corrupt snooping. Reclaiming Blockchain's True Purpose Without Speculative Coins: Delivers mathematical double-entry conservation, non-repudiation, and public timestamp finality on standard object storage at near-$0 transaction cost and zero Proof-of-Work energy waste. Clean-Account Provenance Closure (Zero Hidden Dirty Money): Every credit in a clean account must reference a counter-signed upstream clean transaction or regulated issuance node — dark-silo bribes, cartel proceeds, and unattributed shells fail lineage verification on contact. Symmetric Accountability for Officials & Treasuries: Connects commercial banking directly to WP-0005's public-treasury conservation DAG so corrupt officials cannot siphon public funds or launder off-ledger kickbacks back into the clean economy. Four Graduated Secret-Protection Tiers: Formalizes Tier 1 (blinded clean-standing proof), Tier 2 (PRIVATE .omenc vault), Tier 3 (SECRET protected multi-key custody), and Tier 4 (SECRET | HEADER_ENCRYPTED + .fstab.omenc topology cloaking against insider graph analysis). Defeating Corrupt Agencies ("Watching the Watchmen"): Eliminates unilateral agency backdoors via (t, n) adversarial quorum warrants (Independent Judiciary + Citizen Ombudsman + Regulator), single-leaf Merkle disclosure, and mandatory APPEND_ONLY reverse-audit receipts. all.title: Comparison of Two Dementia Care Interventions and Usual Care on Days Spent at Home: The D‐ CARE Randomized Clinical Trial
all.venue: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
all.abstract: BACKGROUND: Days spent at home (DSAH) is a clinically meaningful patient-centered outcome among persons living with dementia (PLWD). OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether either of two dementia care interventions increased the number of DSAH compared with each other and with usual care. DESIGN: Pragmatic 18-month 3-arm randomized clinical trial conducted from June 2019 through August 2023. SETTING: Four clinical trial sites in North Carolina, Texas, and Pennsylvania. PARTICIPANTS: Total of 1968 (90.4% of 2176) community-living PLWD with complete Medicare data. INTERVENTIONS: Health-system dementia care (HSDC) co-management by advance practice providers, community-based dementia care (CBDC) provided telephonically by a social worker, nurse, or licensed therapist, and usual care (UC), each lasting up to 18 months. MAIN OUTCOME: The number of DSAH was calculated as 546 (i.e., 18 months) minus the number of overnight days in a health care facility and days not alive, using data from Medicare. RESULTS: The percentages of DSAH were 83.5, 84.9, and 83.6 for the HSDC, CBDC, and UC groups, respectively. For each pairwise comparison among the three groups, incidence rate ratios for DSAH approximated 1.0, denoting no differences, and the corresponding mean differences in DSAH were small and not statistically significant: -7.2 (98.3% CI: -31.4 to 17.0) for HSDC versus CBDC; -0.3 (-48.4 to 47.7) for HSDC versus UC; and 6.9 (-41.3 to 55.5) for CBDC versus UC. There were no substantive differences in mean values across the three groups for days in any of the health care facilities. Mean [SD] days not alive were greatest for UC (68.3 [134.4]), followed by HSDC (65.3 [133.3]) and CBDC (60.0 [129.8]). CONCLUSIONS: In this pragmatic randomized clinical trial of dementia care programs, health system-based and community-based interventions did not differ from each other or from usual care in the number of DSAH for PLWD over the 18-month intervention period. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT03786471.

all.title: Цифровые валюты центральных банков в мировой финансовой системе: перспективы цифрового рубля
all.abstract: -Введение. С 2017 по 2024 год число центральных банков, разрабатывающих цифровые валюты (ЦВЦБ), возросло с 35 до 134, охватив 98% мирового ВВП. Статья посвящена системному анализу мирового опыта ЦВЦБ с позиций финансового суверенитета и перспектив развития цифрового рубля. Цель исследования – оценить место России в глобальной ЦВЦБ-архитектуре и разработать рекомендации по развитию цифрового рубля. Материалы и методы. Методология включает сравнительный институциональный анализ 134 юрисдикций, кейс-стади пяти проектов (e-CNY, цифровой евро, цифровой рубль, mBridge, Project Dunbar) и авторский фреймворк «суверенного платѐжного стека» (SPS). Результаты исследования. Выявлено, что 73% ЦВЦБ-проектов реализуют двухуровневую архитектуру; лидирующую позицию занимает Китай (e-CNY: 22,6 млрд CNY-транзакций в 2024 году). Россия (SPS=7,6/10) сохраняет высокий потенциал, однако отстаѐт от Китая по технологическому суверенитету. Установлено, что цифровой рубль способен стать инструментом «мягкой» дедолларизации и укрепления финансового суверенитета в условиях санкций. Обсуждение и заключения. Предложены пять стратегических рекомендаций: ускоренное масштабирование пилота, интеграция в mBridge, внедрение офлайнрежима, развитие открытого API и формирование БРИКС-альянса цифровых валют. Результаты исследования вносят вклад в теорию монетарного суверенитета и имеют практическую значимость для регуляторов и финансовых институтов. Introduction. From 2017 to 2024, the number of central banks developing digital currencies (CBDCs) grew from 35 to 134, covering 98% of global GDP. This article provides a systemic analysis of global CBDC experience from the perspective of financial sovereignty and the prospects for the digital ruble. The study aims to assess Russia's position in the global CBDC architecture and to formulate recommendations for the digital ruble's development. Materials and Methods. The methodology combines comparative institutional analysis of 134 jurisdictions, case studies of five projects (e-CNY, digital euro, digital ruble, mBridge, Project Dunbar), and the authors' proprietary Sovereign Payment Stack (SPS) framework. Results. It is found that 73% of CBDC projects adopt a two-tier architecture; China holds a leading position (e-CNY: 22.6 billion CNY transactions in 2024). Russia (SPS=7.6/10) retains strong potential but lags behind China in technological sovereignty. The digital ruble is identified as a viable tool for "soft" de-dollarisation and strengthening financial sovereignty under sanctions. Discussion and Conclusions. Five strategic recommendations are proposed: accelerated pilot scaling, integration into mBridge, offline-mode implementation, development of an open API, and the formation of a BRICS digital-currency alliance. The findings contribute to the theory of monetary sovereignty and offer practical value for regulators and financial institutions.

all.title: Digital Payments and Cash: Liberty, Inclusion and Institutional Safeguards in the Transition toward a Cash-light Society
all.abstract: The shift to digital payments sparks debate over a fully cash-free society. This paper differentiates a voluntary cash-light society from a coercive cashless one. While digital payments improve efficiency and financial inclusion, forcing the total abandonment of cash brings risks of social exclusion, system fragility and concentrated institutional trust. Advocating monetary pluralism with co-existing payment methods, the paper proposes new payment technologies including CBDC should meet requirements of accessibility, privacy, resilience and freedom of choice. Policies shall secure public access to cash alongside safe digital payment services. Preserving diverse payment options protects citizens’ liberty without opposing technological innovation.

all.title: Regulatory Responses to Private Stablecoins: A Comparative Literature Review of the United States, the European Union, and China's Mainland
institutions: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics
all.abstract: Private stablecoins have been more and more adopted as a medium of payment, for on-chain settlement, and for cross-border transfers. As a result, the genuineness of reserves, the safeguarding of redemption and consumer protection, and anti-money laundering and cross-border transmission of risk are top regulatory issues. In this article, we will be discussing only those payment stablecoins which are backed by fiat currency. Adopting a structured narrative review alongside a functional comparative approach, it considers the relevant regulatory frameworks and the scholarship of the United States, China (including its license in Hong Kong) and the European Union. Some key takeaways from the findings are that the United States implements compliant issuance through a licensed system and a dual federal-state regulatory framework, that the European Union (EU) regulates compliant issuance using a classification framework under MiCA and that China's mainland employs a prohibition-based regulatory framework on the issuance of compliant products, supported by risk monitoring and interagency coordination. The banking sector, the digital-asset industry, coordination among EU Member States as well as the issue of monetary sovereignty also have an impact on the formation and assessment of these regimes. The Travel Rule is still being implemented unevenly, and anti-money laundering information needs and cross-border data transfer restrictions are still conflicting, while the authority and accountability of regulators remain a challenge. Competition with payment stablecoins serves as further evidence of the complex link between payment innovation, bank credit, and financial stability, in that it is dependent on particular institutional conditions. As the regimes have been in operation for too brief a period to achieve a long-term ranking, evidence from these regimes remains limited and intermittent. The clarification of the conceptual and legal line between the digital renminbi, tokenized deposits and private stablecoins could still be in the queue for the China's mainland, as well as improving the tools of risk classification and monitoring, stress scenarios, cross-border information exchange and allocation of responsibilities.

all.title: Криптоактивы и термодинамический паразитизм: Эксергетический аудит доказательства работы (PROOF-OF-WORK), цифрового рубля и цифровой ренты
all.abstract: Статья дополняет прикладной цикл исследований макроэкономических и термодинамических границ современных монетарно-рентных моделей [1–3] и связывает его с методологией фрактальной развёртки и эксергетического учёта [4–6]. В работе проведён физико-математический и балансовый аудит криптоэкономики и государственных цифровых валют (CBDC). Доказано, что децентрализованные криптовалюты на базе консенсуса Proof-of-Work (майнинг) представляют собой прямую инверсию второго начала термодинамики и эталонный образец «деструктивного труда» с нулевым коэффициентом негэнтропии (K_нг = 0): высокопотенциальная электроэнергия с эксергией, близкой к 100%, сжигается для перебора криптографических хэшей без создания материального или информационного порядка, целиком превращаясь в сбросовое тепло и электронный мусор. На основе двухуровневой модели собственности вскрыт механизм паразитирования майнинг-индустрии на общественной энергетической инфраструктуре базового уровня, провоцирующий дефицит мощностей для реального сектора и ускоряющий падение интегрального EROI цивилизации. Показано, что эволюция криптоактивов в сторону консенсуса Proof-of-Stake (PoS) и стейблкоинов воспроизводит формулу экспоненциального ссудного процента и привязывает цифровой контур к пирамиде государственного долга США. Отдельный аудит проведён в отношении цифрового рубля Банка России (запущенного в массовый оборот в сентябре 2026 г.): показано, что при техническом потенциале «окрашивания» целевых средств он остаётся фиатным обязательством без эксергетического обеспечения, а обсуждаемое регулятором в ноябре 2026 г. введение процентов на остаток и кредитования в цифровых рублях возвращает платформу в ловушку «процентной эмиссии». Обоснованы инженерно-институциональные меры по санации энергетического и цифрового контуров. При подготовке текста использовался генеративный ИИ (DeepSeek) для структурирования и редактуры. Автор несёт полную ответственность за содержание работы.

all.title: Digital laggard, FinTech Frontrunner? Neobanks and the paradox of Digital Adoption in Bulgaria
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
institutions: University of Finance, Business and Entrepreneurship
all.abstract: This paper examines the co-existence of rapid social digitalization, limited internet banking use, and rapid penetration of mobile first banking platforms in Bulgaria. Drawing on post-Keynesian banking theory, FinTech research, and the literature on post-socialist banking transformation, it identifies a substantial gap between digital connectivity and digital financial participation, persistent regional unevenness, and functional unbundling of the banking relationship. The evidence suggests that neobanks first contest the transactional interface, while incumbent banks retain greater importance in deposits, income flows, and credit for the (real) economy. The paper interprets this as an emerging transformation and adaption of banking relationships in Bulgaria’s post-socialist economy.

all.title: Disrupting the status quo: Fintech startups, incumbent banks and gender diversity
all.abstract: Purpose The disruption posed by Fintech startups threatens traditional banking models, making it imperative to understand how incumbent banks react and adapt through Fintech adoption. The study aims to uncover how such disruptive pressure shapes banks’ adoption of Fintech and the moderating impact of board gender diversity in this adaptive response. Design/methodology/approach Using a panel random-effect model, this study examines data from Nifty-listed banks over 2015–2023, combined with data on Fintech startup activity. Additional robustness checks were conducted to ensure the stability of the findings. Findings The results show that Fintech startups positively drive banks’ Fintech adoption, reflecting a form of constructive destruction in which disruptive entrants compel incumbents to adapt rather than displace them. Accordingly, board gender diversity negatively moderates this relationship, reflecting that gender-diverse boards may adopt a more rigorous and effective decision-making under disruptive conditions. Robustness checks validate these findings, indicating consistent results across different points of the conditional distribution. Research limitations/implications The research is limited to large-cap Indian Banks and treats Fintech activity in aggregate, without distinguishing between lending and payments. Future research could explore sub-sectoral and cross-country variations. Originality/value The study advances the literature by conceptualizing Fintech startups as catalysts of gradual and adaptive change within incumbent banks, while linking women’s representation in corporate governance to banks’ innovation strategies under Fintech disruption.

all.title: The role of bank FinTech adoption in the profitability of Indian commercial banks
all.abstract: This study investigates the multidimensional impact of internal Financial Technology (FinTech) adoption on the financial performance of commercial banks in an emerging market context, specifically aiming to examine how institutional characteristics like bank size and ownership structure mediate the financial realization of digital transformation. Utilizing a panel dataset of 29 Indian commercial banks from 2016 to 2024, a novel, multidimensional FinTech development index is constructed via text-mining of bank annual reports, encompassing Information Transfer, Payments and Settlements, and Technical Base. Employing a Fixed Effects model with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and a dynamic two-step system GMM estimator to address potential endogeneity and reverse causality, the empirical results reveal that internal FinTech adoption exerts a significant, lagged negative impact on overall bank profitability. Heterogeneity analyses demonstrate that this immediate, 1-year lagged profitability shock is heavily concentrated within large banks and private sector institutions, whereas small and state-owned banks experience no statistically significant decline. These findings suggest that the massive, immediate capital expenditures required to remain competitive against agile FinTech entrants create a distinct short-term structural drag on the performance of private institutions. Consequently, bank executives should anticipate a short-term profitability dip, avoiding premature cuts to technological investments, and instead pivot strategic focus toward human capital upskilling. By highlighting the transitional friction institutions face when upgrading digital systems, this research provides critical insights for advancing Sustainable Development Goal 9 regarding resilient infrastructure. Furthermore, policymakers should consider phased regulatory compliance timelines to ease the intense capital transition for commercial banks.

all.title: Islamic financial literacy as a driver of fintech adoption in Indonesia: An empirical investigation
all.abstract: Despite offering greater accessibility and transaction efficiency, the market penetration of Islamic fintech services remains suboptimal. This issue may be attributed to several factors that have not yet been comprehensively identified. This study aims to examine the adoption behaviour of Islamic fintech services by extending the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) through the integration of Islamic Digital Financial Literacy (IDFL) and Perceived Risk (PR). Data were collected from 377 Islamic fintech users in Indonesia and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to examine the relationships among Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Social Influence, Facilitating Conditions, Islamic Digital Financial Literacy, Behavioural Intention, and Use Behaviour. The findings reveal that Performance Expectancy, Facilitating Conditions, Social Influence, and Islamic Digital Financial Literacy have positive and significant effects on Behavioural Intention to use Islamic fintech services, thereby confirming the relevance of the extended UTAUT framework in this context. However, Effort Expectancy and Perceived Risk do not exhibit significant effects on Behavioural Intention. Furthermore, Behavioural Intention is identified as the strongest predictor of Use Behaviour, highlighting its dominant role in driving the actual adoption of Islamic fintech services. These findings indicate that users’ perceptions of performance benefits, ease of use, social influence, and digital financial literacy grounded in Islamic principles constitute the key drivers of Islamic fintech adoption. This study offers important implications for Islamic fintech service providers and policymakers seeking to strengthen the position of Islamic fintech as a trusted provider of Islamic financial services. The findings underscore the critical role of Islamic Digital Financial Literacy among Islamic fintech users; therefore, managers should develop policies that enhance public understanding of Islamic fintech services and their products. In addition, policymakers are expected to strengthen data security assurance in order to increase consumer trust in Islamic fintech platforms.

all.title: The Influence of Fintech Adoption on Financial Inclusion and Economic Growth in Emerging Economies
all.venue: International Journal of Innovations in Science Engineering and Management.
all.abstract: Fintech adoption is transforming financial systems in emerging economies by expanding access to digital payments, mobile banking, digital lending, and other financial services. This review examines the influence of fintech adoption on financial inclusion and economic growth, focusing on its benefits, challenges, and policy implications. The reviewed literature indicates that fintech can improve access to banking, savings, credit, and remittances, particularly among underserved populations and small businesses. It can also support entrepreneurship, reduce transaction costs, improve financial efficiency, and contribute to economic development. However, cybersecurity threats, data privacy concerns, irresponsible digital lending, and unequal digital access may limit these benefits. Effective regulation, consumer protection, digital infrastructure, and financial education are therefore essential for responsible fintech development. The review highlights the importance of inclusive digital financial systems in promoting equitable financial access and sustainable economic growth across emerging economies.

all.title: Beyond Adoption: A Critical Analysis of Fintech and Sustainable Performance in Pakistan's SMEs
all.venue: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development
all.abstract: Fintech solutions are considered highly beneficial for SMEs in developing economies. In Pakistan, millions of merchants can now access digital payment infrastructure, and several recent studies demonstrate positive effects of fintech on firms. This paper provides a critical review of this literature. While many benefits are presented it is argued that there is limited evidence for long-term sustainable benefits (economic, environmental and social) from fintech. Using recently published empirical studies alongside official data from the State Bank of Pakistan, we show how the literature has significant limitations. These include 1) theoretical assumptions around adoption stopping short of actual adoption, 2) Cross-sectional design and self-reporting, 3) A limited understanding of sustainability, often measured perceptually, and 4) Inconsistent statistical data based on context. We conclude that whilst digital payments are necessary, SMEs gaining credit, documentation and capacity will determine long-term performance through fintech. Longitudinal, mixed-method and comparative across sector research should be conducted.

all.title: Regulatory compliance and behavioural drivers of fintech adoption for financial inclusion in India
all.venue: American International Journal of Humanities Arts and Social Sciences
all.abstract: Financial technology (FinTech) has widened access to payments, credit and insurance and supports financial inclusion and sustainable development, yet adoption remains uneven because users weigh digital trust and perceived risk against convenience. Research on the behavioural determinants of adoption and research on FinTech regulation have developed separately, so the way regulatory compliance shapes user behaviour is poorly explained. This study examines how regulatory compliance and behavioural attributes influence the adoption of FinTech services in India. It employs a qualitative, integrative literature synthesis with thematic content analysis of 67 secondary sources, comprising 57 scholarly publications, five official and institutional publications and five Indian statutes, of which 41 were published between 2024 and 2026. The results show six dominant theoretical lenses and eight recurring behavioural attributes: digital trust, perceived risk, financial and digital literacy, financial self-efficacy, loss aversion, herd behaviour, overconfidence and mental accounting. Of the 15 studies in the synthesis matrix, 10 include trust or perceived risk, whereas only three include government or regulatory support explicitly. India's compliance architecture rests on four regulators and six legal instruments covering payment authorisation, electronic transactions, anti-money laundering, digital identity, personal data protection and digital lending. The findings suggest that regulatory compliance acts as institutional assurance that works indirectly, by raising digital trust and lowering perceived risk, and is not a direct driver of adoption. Literacy and self-efficacy strengthen this pathway, while loss aversion weakens it. Two of the four propositions are supported and two are partly supported, because privacy risk and literacy show inconsistent effects. JEL Classification Codes: G21, G28, G41, K23, O33.

all.title: AI Adoption and Startup Valuation: An Empirical Analysis of Fintech and Financial Services Firms
all.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and startup valuation in fintech and financial services firms using a sample of 287 companies with 897 funding rounds from January 2020 to June 2026. Employing OLS regression with firm fixed effects, we estimate that AI-adopting firms command valuation premiums of 38-48% (β = 0.405, t = 5.8, p < 0.001) compared to non-AI peers, even after controlling for funding stage, prior financing, company age, sector, and geography. The premium persists across all specifications and increases substantially during market downturns (β = 0.48 in 2022-2023 vs. β = 0.18 in 2020-2021), suggesting AI adoption serves as a quality signal when capital is constrained. Sectoral analysis reveals heterogeneous effects, with largest premiums in payments (+52%) and embedded finance (+48%), consistent with Resource-Based View theory predicting that AI provides competitive advantages where it creates differential product capabilities. Endogeneity concerns are addressed through instrumental variable analysis using exposure to AI-focused universities as an exogenous shock to AI talent availability, which yields similar estimates (β = 0.42, robust to alternative specifications). Our findings establish AI adoption as a critical value driver in financial services innovation, with implications for startup strategy, investor valuation models, and understanding technology diffusion in regulated industries.

all.title: Competition and Bank Stability in China: The Role of Fintech under Nonlinear and Threshold Effects
all.abstract: This study examines the Chinese banking sector over the period 2010–2022 and constructs a bank-level fintech index alongside a macro-level digital finance measure. Using generalised method of moments and panel threshold models, it investigates the relationship between competition, fintech, and bank stability inefficiency. The results indicate a significant non-linear effect of competition on risk, supporting the competition–stability hypothesis. Threshold analyses identify single- and double-threshold effects for capital adequacy and diversification. At the fintech level, macro-level development is associated with a significant reduction in bank risk and exhibits stronger effects than bank-level fintech. In contrast, bank-level fintech appears to mitigate risk only under specific conditions (e.g. high capitalisation or strong competition), suggesting context-dependent effects. Overall, the findings indicate that balanced market competition and stronger macro-level fintech development improve bank stability. The results further suggest that maintaining an appropriate level of competition, strengthening capital adequacy, and promoting a robust fintech ecosystem may enhance financial stability.

all.title: Fintech adoption and its impact on climate smart agriculture technology adoption and agricultural productivity in rice and maize farming
all.abstract: Farmers have an increasing need for financial resources, which has led to the development and adoption of Fintech. This research aims to identify the determinants of Fintech adoption and productivity of rice and maize cultivation, and to examine how Fintech affects farmers’ intensity of climate-smart agricultural (CSA) technologies in transforming the agro-economy. Fintech and CSA technologies may contribute to climate adaptation and sustainable agricultural development, contributing to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 2 and 13 by improving agricultural productivity and climate resilience. To evaluate the effect of Fintech on rice and maize production, the study was conducted with 240 rural households through a cross-sectional survey in Kaliganj and Kaliakair Upazilas of Gazipur District, Bangladesh. A fractional regression model, an instrumental variable fractional regression model, and a Cobb–Douglas production function were employed. bKash, Rocket, and Nagad were among the preferred Fintech technologies. Education, remittances, number of mobile phones, Fintech adoption, and family size significantly influenced CSA adoption intensity, although remittance was significant only for rice and family size was not significant in the instrumental variable fractional regression model. Rice and maize yields were significantly influenced by family size, number of mobile phones, remittance receipt, and Fintech adoption, while fertilizer and hybrid variety use significantly influenced rice yield. Government and non-government organizations should strengthen rural financial infrastructure, promote Fintech and CSA adoption, and prioritize digital literacy and financial awareness in line with SDG 9, 2, and 13. This research expands understanding of how Fintech influences CSA practices among rice and maize farmers.

all.title: DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY ADOPTION IN MICROENTERPRISES: A BIBLIOMETRIC AND THEMATIC REVIEW OF DIGITAL MARKETING AND FINTECH RESEARCH
all.venue: International Journal of Small and Medium Enterprises
all.abstract: Microenterprises are a fundamental component of economic development in emerging economies because they generate employment, foster innovation, and contribute to GDP. However, their limited resources make it difficult to keep pace with the rapidly expanding digital economy, and research on their adoption of digital marketing and financial technology (FinTech) remains fragmented. This study examines the evolution and thematic structure of the literature on digital marketing and FinTech adoption in microenterprises. Following the PRISMA guidelines, 499 records published between 2010 and 2026 were retrieved from the Scopus database using two search strings; after duplicate and ineligible records were removed, 337 documents were subjected to bibliometric analysis, and 159 full-text documents were reviewed thematically. The results show that the field grew at an annual rate of 26.87%, with an average document age of 2.16 years and 17.42 citations per document. The documents were written by 1,123 authors, and journal articles accounted for 68.84% (232 documents). The 985 author keywords formed three co-occurrence clusters centered on digital marketing, FinTech and financial inclusion, and FinTech adoption and financial literacy. The findings of this study suggest that the field is young, fast-growing, and highly collaborative and that it converges on four themes: digital marketing adoption and performance transformation; FinTech-driven financial inclusion and entrepreneurial development; financial literacy, FinTech adoption, and sustainable business development; and the strategic integration of digital technologies for marketing performance. Research attention has shifted from internet-based marketing toward FinTech adoption, financial inclusion, and the digital economy, whereas digital marketing remains a basic but less developed theme. JEL Classification Codes: G23, L26, M31, O33.

all.title: Gender differences in fintech adoption among Indian millennials for financial inclusion and sustainable development
all.abstract: Digital financial technology has become a key channel for financial inclusion in India, yet women are less likely than men to translate their willingness to use FinTech into actual use, slowing progress toward gender equality and sustainable development. This study examines how perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, user innovativeness and security concerns shape millennials' intention to adopt FinTech, whether that intention carries through to actual adoption and whether gender changes the strength of this path. The study employs cross-sectional survey data from 397 millennials in Uttar Pradesh, India, between August and November 2025, and analyses them with the PROCESS macro (Model 14) in SPSS using 5,000 bootstrap resamples. The results show that perceived ease of use (β = 0.759), perceived usefulness (β = 0.708), user innovativeness (β = 0.676) and security concerns (β = 0.259) raise intention to adopt (p < .001), and that intention strongly predicts adoption (β = 0.736 to 0.927). The direct effect of security concerns on adoption is not significant (β = 0.007, p = .809). Indirect effects are larger for men than for women for ease of use (0.586 against 0.358), usefulness (0.570 against 0.361), innovativeness (0.497 against 0.271) and security concerns (0.240 against 0.165), and all four indices of moderated mediation are negative and significant (−0.229, −0.209, −0.226 and −0.075). The findings suggest that intention is the mechanism through which user perceptions translate into FinTech adoption and that this mechanism operates more weakly among women, although women made up 60% of the sample. JEL Classification Codes: G21, G23, G41, G53, J16, O33.

all.title: The Impact of Fintech Adoption on Firms’ Sustainable Performance: Evidence from SMEs in Saudi Arabia
all.abstract: This study investigates whether the use of financial technology (Fintech) is linked to better sustainability outcomes among Saudi Arabian small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), while examining employee efficiency as a mediating mechanism and employee digital literacy (EDL) as a moderating condition. Data were obtained from questionnaire responses from 265 manufacturing SMEs operating in Saudi Arabia. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was employed to test the hypothesized paths, including the indirect pathway involving employee efficiency and the interaction with EDL. The estimates show favorable direct associations between Fintech adoption and the economic, environmental, and social pillars of firm performance, as well as indirect associations operating through employee efficiency. The Fintech–efficiency association is also significantly conditioned by EDL. Evidence from the Saudi manufacturing industry broadens the predominantly service-oriented Fintech literature and sheds light on the organizational processes connecting digital finance with sustainability. For managers, the findings point to the value of combining Fintech implementation with initiatives that enable employees to perform their work more efficiently and effectively.

all.title: Sustaining Merchant Fintech Adoption: Empirical Insights Into Retailer Satisfaction With UPI And Mobile Payment Ecosystems
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The growth of the real-time digital payment ecosystem has changed the way commercial transactions have been conducted in India, largely thanks to the acceptance of the Unified Payments System (UPI). In this environment, retailers are the linchpins whose acceptance of and satisfaction with cashless payments are essential to keeping it alive. The determinants and level of merchant satisfaction towards mobile payment application is an empirical study in the Coimbatore city which is a leading industrial and commercial city in the state of Tamilnadu. A structured questionnaire that allowed the use of a Likert scale was used to collect primary data from 96 active retailers from January to February 2026. The overall degree of merchant satisfaction is high, with 71.9% of them indicating high satisfaction level, as revealed by the statistical evaluation using Cronbach's Alpha, Simple Percentage Analysis, Chi-Square Testing and the Weighted Average Method. Transaction ease (mean score: 4.39) and operational efficiency (mean score: 4.25) are the major determinants of satisfaction and satisfaction scores are similar across enterprises based on workforce size (χ² = 6.12, df = 6, p > 0.05). While Google Pay (40.6%), PhonePe (20.8%) and Paytm (19.8%) have strong platform preference, there is some network instability, transaction settlement delays and perceived security risks at the time of using these platforms. The study ends with practical recommendations for the FinTech service providers and the policymakers to improve the grievance redressal and backend resiliency of the merchants.

all.title: Exploring the Potential of Fintech Adoption in Advancing Green Economic Growth in Indonesia: An Initial Concept and Perspective
all.venue: Advances in economics, business and management research/Advances in Economics, Business and Management Research
all.abstract: This paper will explore the potential of Financial Technology (Fintech) implementation to boost the Indonesian green economic growth, emphasizing its use in promoting sustainable financial inclusion, enhancing access to green investment, and supporting environmentally responsible innovation. This phenomenon coincides with the country’s increasing commitment to promoting a green economy as part of its sustainable development agenda. However, the challenge lies in how fintech adoption can be effectively aligned with environmental objectives to generate inclusive and sustainable economic growth. Many fintech initiatives in Indonesia remain focused on financial inclusion and efficiency, with limited emphasis on ecological sustainability and green investment. This study employs a conceptual and qualitative descriptive approach, synthesizing literature, policy documents, and existing data on fintech and green economy frameworks in Indonesia.

all.title: FinTech Competition, Deposit Funding Costs, and Bank Interest Margins: The Role of Digital Transformation in China
all.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
all.abstract: Purpose: To examine how FinTech competitive exposure relates to customer deposit funding costs and net interest margins, and whether digital investment conditions these relationships in Chinese banking. Method: Public annual reports provide 48 bank year records for eight listed Chinese banking groups during 2019–2024. The primary financial analysis uses 32 observations for 2020–2023. Lagged investment models use 26 observations from seven banks. Competitive exposure combines the 2019 retail deposit share with changes in the Peking University provincial digital payment index. Bank and year fixed effects, bank cluster intervals, an enumerated wild bootstrap and influence analyses assess conditional relationships. Findings: Mean net interest margin falls from 2.299% in 2019 to 1.790% in 2023, while mean deposit cost rises from 1.809% to 1.901%. None of the five hypotheses receives clear support. The digital interaction is negative for deposit costs and margins, but both intervals span zero. Measurement choices, differential trends and influential banks limit interpretation. Originality/Implications: This pilot study provides an exploratory, accounting-based framework for jointly examining external digital payment development, reported deposit funding costs, technology investment and net interest margins. Its transparent measurement and disclosure procedures offer a basis for extending the analysis to more diverse banking institutions. The findings do not establish that technology expenditure protects interest margins under FinTech competition.

all.title: Bridging the Last Mile: A Necessity-Driven and Risk-Inversion Framework for FinTech Adoption in Emerging Markets
all.venue: Journal of Accounting Business and Management (JABM)
