Low capacity justifies restricting AI to assistive functions; it does not justify weaker safeguards for gatekeeping ones.The framework is normative and should be tested. We propose five questions.• RQ1. Do false-rejection rates of biometric visitor verification differ by age, skin tone, disability and device quality, and does a manual fallback close the resulting gap in completed visits? Laboratory testing already shows demographic differentials across face-recognition algorithms (Grother et al., 2019). Design: disaggregated audit of operational logs.• RQ2. Does introducing an AI-assisted pathway change completed visits, cancellations and inperson visit numbers? Design: stepped-wedge rollout across facilities. • RQ3. How often do reviewers override automated flags, and does this change with time pressure and access to underlying evidence? Design: log analysis of staff interviews. • RQ4. Which explanation formats enable families to identify and correct errors? Design:randomised vignette experiments with visitors. • RQ5. Does same-session review reduce irreversible relational harm compared with retrospective appeal? Design: comparison of family-reported visit quality and appeal outcomes across sites.Evaluation should combine security indicators with relational and procedural outcomes, report who is excluded, and involve incarcerated people and families in defining success.AI is not inherently incompatible with humane visitation. It may reduce delays, improve translation and extend contact when travel is impossible. The test is institutional purpose and the affected person's practical capacity to understand, challenge and correct an outcome before relational harm becomes irreversible. Preserve in-person visitation; use video to expand contact; tier AI functions by consequence; prohibit solely automated adverse decisions; and measure success by whether families keep safe, dignified and meaningful contact.

all.title: Advanced Customer Service Chatbot with Intent Classification and Sentiment Analysis
all.abstract: In an era of rapidly evolving customer expectations and increasing digital interactions, the demand for intelligent, responsive, and emotionally aware customer service solutions has intensified. This paper introduces an advanced customer service chatbot framework that synergizes intent classification and sentiment analysis to enable natural, accurate, and empathetic user communication. Our chatbot system combines two powerful AI technologies to understand users better than ever. First, a hybrid CNN-LSTM model pinpoints the exact purpose behind a user's message with high accuracy. At the same time, a BERT-based sentiment analysis model decodes the emotional tone of the query whether the user is frustrated, excited, or neutral. Together, these tools let the chatbot craft responses that aren’t just accurate but also emotionally aware, making interactions feel more personal and thoughtful. To build and test this system, we used real-world datasets packed with thousands of labeled customer questions, each tagged with their intent (e.g., “complaint” or “purchase inquiry”) and sentiment (e.g., “positive” or “urgent”). When compared to older chatbots like rule-based systems or those using just one AI model our approach scored higher across the board: accuracy, recall, and F1-score all saw significant boosts.

all.title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
all.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to trust and user satisfaction. Trust and user satisfaction are positively related to intention to continue using. The results of this study can contribute both theoretically and practically to modern AI chatbot quality evaluation models.

all.title: Can Chatbots Replace Human Relationships? Conversational AI, Service Authenticity, and Customer Experience Management in Digital Services: A Narrative Review
all.abstract: This narrative review examines whether conversational AI chatbots can substitute for human relationships in digital services by synthesizing recent evidence on perceived service authenticity, trust formation, and customer experience outcomes. Drawing on literature published between approximately 2020 and 2025 across experiments, surveys, qualitative studies, and conceptual papers in banking, retail, tourism, hospitality, healthcare, and customer support contexts, the review shows that customers evaluate chatbots not only by efficiency or information quality but also by empathy, warmth, humanness, and social attentiveness, which together shape perceived authenticity and relational quality. Across service settings, trust emerges as the dominant mechanism linking chatbot quality to satisfaction, loyalty, continuance intention, and brand outcomes. However, the evidence also reveals clear limits: chatbots perform best in routine, low-emotion, competence-driven tasks, while human agents outperform them in emotionally charged, complaint-oriented, privacy-sensitive, and complex interactions. The review argues that chatbots are better understood as relationship emulators than relationship replacements and that hybrid human–AI service models currently offer the most credible design for customer experience management. Managerially, firms should automate routine requests, design for authenticity and trust, and maintain transparent escalation to human agents for high-stakes encounters. Overall confidence in these conclusions is high, given strong thematic convergence across the evidence base.

all.title: Evolving Green Brand Financial and Banking Services Strategy with AI Chatbots: a Cross-National Study of Commercial Banks in Vietnam and Australia
institutions: University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City

all.title: Beyond the Algorithm: How Digital Literacy and Trust Moderate the Association Between Chatbot Quality and Customer Satisfaction in Arab Banking
all.abstract: Artificial-intelligence chatbots are an important retail-banking interface, but customers may not convert perceived technical quality into satisfaction uniformly. This study examines whether self-assessed digital literacy and trust moderate the chatbot-quality–satisfaction association in Arab banking. Survey responses were collected from 700 experienced banking-chatbot users in seven countries between February and May 2026. Four-factor confirmatory factor analysis, country and survey-language invariance tests, hierarchical regression with country fixed effects and HC3 standard errors, and 5,000 respondent bootstrap resamples were employed. Chatbot quality was positively associated with satisfaction (b = 0.312, p < 0.001). The digital-literacy interaction (b = 0.135, p < 0.001) and trust interaction (b = 0.093, p = 0.005) jointly added 3.44 percentage points of explained variance. Digital-literacy moderation remained positive and statistically significant across the reported sensitivity checks. Trust moderation was supported in the primary and bank-cluster inference models but was sensitive to quadratic adjustment, Arabic-only estimation, alternative satisfaction content, and joint empirical-Bayes scoring. Below-threshold average variance extracted, cross-sectional self-reports, and nonprobability sampling constrain interpretation. The findings identify conditional associations rather than intervention effects and support the pilot evaluation of literacy-sensitive interface design and calibrated trust governance.

all.title: A GeoAI-Enhanced LLM Chatbot for EV Charging Services
all.abstract: This study introduces an intelligent chatbot for electric vehicle (EV) charging service providers, which integrates large language models (LLMs) with geospatial data to improve customer service, operational efficiency, and overall service intelligence. By combining prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and geographic information system (GIS) capabilities, the chatbot effectively addresses customer inquiries and supports maintenance decisions across diverse knowledge domains. The system incorporates functions that minimize manual data pre-processing. For optimizing charging station inspection routes, the study implements and compares nearest neighbor and greedy insertion algorithms. Results demonstrate that the nearest neighbor algorithm yields efficient routes when station locations are clustered and inspection priorities are well-defined, reducing travel distance. Integrated with OpenStreetMap (OSM) and built upon a service blueprint, the chatbot delivers advanced geographic information features such as real-time navigation and station availability updates, highlighting the potential of chatbot technologies combined with map services and decision intelligence to establish a geospatial artificial intelligence (GeoAI) foundation for interdisciplinary research and applications.

all.title: The impact of Generative AI chatbots on behavioral intention in travel planning: A theory of consumption value perspective
all.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) chatbots are revolutionizing online travel planning by transitioning travelers’ focus from merely gathering information to obtaining personalized recommendations and facilitating seamless bookings. Grounded in the Interactive Technology Acceptance Model and Consumption Value Theory, this study investigates how the attributes of GenAI chatbots, specifically personalization and anthropomorphism, alongside user traits such as self-efficacy and personal innovativeness, influence travel planning intention through perceived value. Data collected from a questionnaire survey were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The findings reveal that GenAI chatbot attributes (personalization and anthropomorphism) and user traits (self-efficacy and personal innovativeness) exert significant direct positive effects on perceived values. The indirect effects of anthropomorphism, personalization, self-efficacy, and personal innovativeness on adoption intentions are most pronounced through hedonic value, followed by utilitarian value, with novelty value playing the least prominent mediating role. This study enriches the theoretical understanding of AI-based customer service and provides tourism businesses with insights into enhancing GenAI’s features and shaping consumer perceptions.

all.title: Customer Service Accessibility on the Websites of 100 Large Nordic Consumer Brands, 2026
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: How do large Nordic consumer brands present customer service on their public websites? On 21 November 2026 we loaded the home page and first-level customer-service, contact and help pages of 100 consumer-facing companies in Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Finland (25 per country, six sectors) in an automated browser and recorded 13 indicators. 91 sites could be measured. Key findings (n=91): 97% link to a help centre or FAQ. 86% offer chat. 43% present an AI chatbot or virtual assistant, often under a human first name such as Telmi, Sonja or Nova. 59% state opening hours. 29% state weekend hours. 56% show a phone number. 38% show a customer-service e-mail address on these pages. AI chatbots were most common in telecom (69%) and travel/transport (70%). The sample is purposive and the measures cover only public, first-level pages. Dataset, manual-review log and code are included. Competing interests: the author's company develops customer-service software.

all.title: The Effect of AI-Powered Chatbots on Customer Satisfaction: A Systematic Literature Review Comparing AI with Human and Rule-Based Agents
all.abstract: AI-powered chatbots now handle a large share of digital customer service, yet whether they satisfy customers as well as human agents or older rule-based systems remains disputed, and the evidence is scattered. Objective. Where earlier reviews of service chatbots have centred on adoption and acceptance, this review conditions inclusion on the presence of a service comparator and therefore addresses satisfaction as the comparative judgement it actually is. It synthesises empirical research published from January 2022 to the final search date of 26 June 2026 on how AI chatbots affect customer satisfaction relative to human agents and rule-based chatbots, and on the factors, mechanisms, and service models that shape that effect. Methods. Following PRISMA 2020, searches of six databases returned 849 records; after deduplication and two-stage PICOTQ screening requiring a comparison with a human agent or rule-based chatbot, 47 empirical studies were retained, of which 37 provide direct comparisons and 10 an implicit contrast. Quality was appraised with the MMAT 2018 and the evidence combined through narrative thematic synthesis. Results. Across the direct comparisons most findings are context-dependent rather than uniform. Human agents perform better on affective and relational outcomes such as empathy and warmth, while chatbots achieve comparable or better results in clearly defined transactional and information-search tasks. Perceived empathy is the dominant mechanism behind the gap; anthropomorphic design narrows it but can rebound after service failure; and trust governs whether customers stay with the chatbot or switch to a human. Hybrid arrangements are the most promising direction, but only three of the 47 studies test one against both pure alternatives, and evidence against rule-based systems rests on two studies. Conclusion. Whether a chatbot satisfies depends on the task, the customer, and the outcome rather than on the technology alone. The review offers a contingency account built on an efficiency-empathy tension, an evidence-based deployment matrix, and an agenda on cultural, longitudinal, and generative-AI gaps.

all.title: Humanizing the Bot: How Conversational AI Responsiveness and Perceived Anthropomorphism Mitigate Customer Decision Hesitation Through Brand Trust
all.venue: International Journal of Economics Management and Accounting (IJEMA)
all.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots in e-commerce has restructured customer service delivery. However, online shoppers frequently experience pre-purchase decision hesitation due to transaction uncertainties. Grounded in Uncertainty Reduction Theory and Social Response Theory, this study investigates how Conversational AI Responsiveness and Perceived Anthropomorphism mitigate Customer Decision Hesitation through the mediating role of Brand Trust. Data were collected via an online survey from 195 e-commerce consumers in Indonesia who interacted with AI chatbots during their shopping journeys. The empirical framework was evaluated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The empirical results reveal that both Conversational AI Responsiveness (β=0.482,p<0.001) and Perceived Anthropomorphism (β=0.325,p<0.001) significantly foster Brand Trust, while directly and indirectly mitigating Customer Decision Hesitation. Furthermore, Brand Trust operates as a vital complementary mediating mechanism (β=-0.395,p<0.001). The structural model explains 51.4 percent of the variance in Brand Trust and 48.7 percent in Customer Decision Hesitation. This research advances Marketing Technology literature by elucidating how humanized AI interactions alleviate choice anxiety, providing strategic guidelines for digital retailers to curb cart abandonment.

all.title: Measuring Consumer Cultural Intelligence and Customer Satisfaction through AI Chatbot Service with the Mediating Role of Communication: Evidence from Shopee Users in Malaysia
all.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
institutions: Asia Pacific University of Technology & Innovation
all.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between four dimensions of CQ (metacognitive, cognitive, motivational, and behavioral) and satisfaction with the communication of Shopee's AI chatbots, as well as whether such relationships are statistically explained by the perception of the quality of communication. CQ in a multi-ethnic market, like Malaysia, in customers' encounters with chatbots has been under-researched. The subjects were recruited using purposive and snowball sampling to yield 196 valid responses from Malaysian consumers aged 18 to 24 who used Shopee's chatbot or in-app virtual customer service in the last six months and were sampled quantitatively in a cross-sectional design. There were 35 items on a Likert scale, which measured six constructs, and the data were analyzed using reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and Sobel tests in SPSS. All constructs were reliable (? = .803–.852). The four CQ dimensions accounted for 58.0% of the variance in satisfaction, with motivational (? = .383), metacognitive (? = .357), behavioral (? = .162), and cognitive (? = .130) CQ having the largest standardized beta coefficients. The quality of communication was strongly correlated with satisfaction (r = .714), and Sobel tests were significant for all four dimensions of CQ (all between Z = 5.71 and 6.31, p < .001), with bootstrap confidence intervals excluding zero and direct effects remaining significant (partial mediation). The construct with the lowest score (M = 2.96) was Satisfaction (M = 2.96), while CQ means ranged between 3.68 and 4.22. The results bring CQ to human-AI service interactions and call for platforms to design for CQ. Since this information is cross-sectional and self-reported, these findings suggest associations, not causal relationships.

all.title: Studying the Influence of AI-Powered Customer Service on Entrepreneurial Performance and Effectiveness
all.abstract: Entrepreneurship has inevitable and crucial role to play in an economy for the benefits it brings in the form of increased employment opportunities, improved GDP growth rate and lifestyle of the citizens. On the other hand, undeniably, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging as a cutting-edge technology impacting almost all domains of every sector. For the reason of this development in the market, it has become need of the hour for each organization or industry to incorporate Artificial Intelligence (AI) into its operations to reap the benefits of cost saving, improved efficiency and reduced human errors. Customer service is an important aspect where all the service providers can amplify the loyalty factor by earning competitive edge in the market. An entrepreneur attempts to hold and expand his stake in market which can be achieved through efficient customer service. The other benefits of opting this strategy are earning competitive advantage as well as brand loyalty. Due to enormous rise in number of activities and customers, it has become difficult to attend and serve all the customers because of limited time factor. For this reason, involvement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in customer service is not an exception and various industries are taking its assistance in gaining competitive advantage in the market, thus creating a completely different landscape. Machine learning, one of the components of AI, is brought into picture to enhance the satisfaction level of customers based on which personalized customer service can be offered. Owing to designing and providing tailored services by AI models in the form of interactive chatbots and other forms, AI has become a factor that every entrepreneur in any industry wants to opt as it can be an element to stay ahead in the competition. On the contrary, the significance and value of human involvement in providing customer services cannot be ignored. There are both positives and negatives of involving technology in customer service by the entrepreneurs, but the latter one can be minimized if the process is strategized properly. Integrating AI can play a big role in this as it involves training as a human brain where technology and personalization can be brought together through proper training of the AI models. This study follows extensive literature review impact of involvement of AI in customer service in entrepreneurship while considering different elements such as decision quality, time management, resource management, growth, expansion and effectiveness if opted by entrepreneur. This study focuses on literature review for experiences with AI in customer service and with human interaction. Findings at preliminary stage are indicative of prompt response to customers, readily availability of service and data, and efficiency when Artificial Intelligence is involved into interactive customer service. The findings of this study are in alignment with the existing literature. Maximum positives can be reaped when Artificial Intelligence is applied in customer service in complex problems. This will improve customers’ experience while giving a boost to operational efficiency also. This study will contribute to filling the research gap in analyzing the involvement of AI in direction of customer service in an entrepreneurial setup. Apart from this, this study will provide insights into service providers on how application of Artificial Intelligence in customer service can be optimized to gain maximum benefits based on which, best method can be used. For future research, many other elements affecting customer expectation from AI customer service are unexplored which can be a scope of study in future research.

all.title: Innovative Approaches to Improving Moderation, Listing, Customer Service and Logistics Processes on Electronic Exchange Platforms
all.abstract: This article examines innovative approaches to improving the efficiency of electronic exchange and public procurement platforms through the application of artificial intelligence technologies. Particular attention is paid to the development of an AI-based moderation mechanism for public procurement electronic platforms, automation of standard exchange contract listing procedures, implementation of an intelligent chatbot-consultant system and development of an AI-routing model to optimize logistics operations. The study analyzes the functional capabilities and expected operational effects of these innovations and proposes a phased mechanism for their implementation. The findings demonstrate that the integrated application of artificial intelligence can reduce manual operations, accelerate information processing, improve service quality, enhance transparency and contribute to the optimization of logistics costs.

all.title: Who is the Hero of the Customer Satisfaction Story - AI, Human or Both? A Literature Review in the Context of AI Powered Customer Service
all.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a buzz word in today’s day and age and has become a key driver in increasing customer satisfaction within the customer support journey. Today AI is being used on both customer facing and agent facing aspects of a service intensive business. From conversational AI, chatbots, recommendation engines or assist-agents to robotic process automation, AI is increasing process efficiency, personalisation and scalability. However human factors such as empathy, trust and relationship building are key parts of interactions. This paper aims to look at whether the true "heroes" of customer satisfaction are AI or the people within the organisation. This paper is a qualitative conceptual study looking at a vast number of sources from scholarly papers and case studies to infer that sustainable and consistent customer satisfaction can come from both AI and the people working within the organisation working strategically and harmonically. Alone, neither will be the true hero. AI will act as an important catalyst to operational excellence within an organisation however humans play a key role in ensuring that there is emotional connection, ethical considerations and trust. Customer satisfaction will be a synergistic outcome from AI empowering humans to have empathetic interactions.

all.title: Real-Time Customer Support via Metaverse AI Avatars: Transforming Customer Experience Through Immersive Intelligent Virtual Assistants
all.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
institutions: National Institute of Technology Andhra Pradesh
all.abstract: As the metaverse, Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI), and real-time rendering technologies merge, customer support is evolving from text-based chat systems to persistent virtual spaces where intelligent virtual assistants serve customers. This chapter explores the AI-powered avatars that incorporate natural language processing, affective computing, voice synthesis, and presence to offer personalized, instant, and situated services. Accordingly, the chapter outlines a technical architecture for this technology, contrasts non-immersive and immersive service paradigms, and discusses applications in the retail, banking, telecommunications, hospitality, and health care industries. The chapter also introduces the Immersive Service Experience (ISX) framework.

all.title: Decision Models for Business Customer-Service Triage: Accuracy, Calibration, Out-of-Scope Detection and Cost of Jev, Clef and Perplexity Decider
all.abstract: Firms increasingly route customer requests with language models, and a new class of decision models (Jev, Clef and Perplexity Decider) returns a probability for every option instead of generated text. We benchmarked these models on 10,580 requests from BANKING77, Bitext and CLINC150 and on 2371 requests sent to three deployed chatbots (HINT3), against the probability readout of Qwen3.8-27B (the backbone of Clef and Perplexity Decider), two generative large language models with verbalised confidence, and trained classifiers. Clef raised accuracy over this backbone readout by 14.9 percentage points on BANKING77 and 9.3 points on CLINC150 but not on Bitext (−1.5 points) or the chatbot requests (−4.9 to −23.5); an unquantised readout moved the benchmark gains by at most 0.2 points. Perplexity Decider added 1.2–3.0 points on the benchmarks. The backbone readout was already well calibrated (expected calibration error 0.019–0.041), whereas verbalised confidence was not (0.048–0.166); temperature scaling made Clef and Perplexity Decider better calibrated than it on two benchmarks. With thresholds calibrated to a nominal 1% false-alarm rate on CLINC150 (0.95–0.98% observed on held-out requests), Clef detected 97.1% of out-of-scope requests, against 77.9–82.3% for Jev, Perplexity Decider, the readout and fine-tuned ModernBERT. Reordering options changed 0.8–11.2% of decisions for every model except Clef. Hosted decision APIs cost US$0.006–0.107 per 1000 decisions. We derive guidance on model choice, thresholds and out-of-scope handling.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence and Customer Satisfaction Among Customers of Selected Deposit Money Banks In Southwest Nigeria
all.venue: Forshen Hub International Journal of Economics and Business Management
all.abstract: This study examined the relationship between selected artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled banking services and customer satisfaction among customers of selected deposit money banks in Southwest Nigeria. The study focused on three AI-enabled service categories: chatbots (CBT), automated messaging systems (AMS) and predictive financial offerings (PFO). Customer satisfaction was considered through channel availability, usability, service quality and an overall satisfaction measure. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted. A total of 396 questionnaires were distributed to bank customers; 374 were retrieved and 363 were retained after data cleaning. Descriptive statistics and ordinary least squares regression were used. The regression table in the source manuscript reports positive coefficients for chatbots, automated messaging and predictive financial offerings across the four reported customer-experience outcomes. For overall customer satisfaction, the reported coefficients are 0.277 for chatbots, 0.331 for automated messaging and 0.252 for predictive financial offerings. These estimates suggest positive associations in the reported model, with automated messaging showing the largest coefficient among the three AI-enabled service categories. Because the manuscript’s abstract, narrative results and regression table contain inconsistent coefficient values and sample counts, the numerical findings in this revised abstract must be treated as provisional pending verification against the original SPSS output. The study contributes customer-level evidence on AI-enabled banking services and satisfaction, while recognising limitations associated with convenience sampling and self-reported cross-sectional data.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence and Fraud Detection of Listed Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
all.venue: JOURNAL OF ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
all.abstract: The study examined the impact of artificial intelligence on fraud detection of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria. Fraud detection was used as independent variable while Artificial intelligence was used as the independent variable. The determinants of artificial intelligence in this study will be automated chatbot, deep learning machine, machine learning solutions and natural language processing. The geographical coverage of this study will be in Nigeria. The study will cover 11years spanning from 2012 to 2022; within this period CBN introduced cashless policy into the Nigerian Financial system. More so, a lot of Banks introduced artificial intelligence into their operations within this period. This study employ survey design, Therefore the study employed a survey method of data collection, via a self-administered questionnaire. The data was collected from deposit money banks in Kaduna state. Out of the 14 Listed Deposit money Banks in Nigeria, 10 banks will be selected based on simple random Sampling Technique. The tool will be statistical Package for Statistical sciences (SPSS) version 20. Regression analysis will be used to predict the effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable and also used to either accept or reject null hypothesis. Validity and reliability test will be carried out. The result from Table 4.6 reveals that automated chat boat has a coefficient value of 0.413 and P-value 0.000. This signifies that automated chat boat has a positive and significant influence on deposit money banks. The regression model in Table 4.6 indicated that deep learning machine has a coefficient value 0.212 and P value 0.009. This signified that deep learning machine is positively and significantly impacting fraud detection among deposit money bank. From the Table 4.6 it was observed that machine learning solution has a coefficient value 0.172 and P value 0.069. This shows that machine learning solution is positively but not significant in detecting fraud. From the Table 4.6 the finding shows that natural learning process has a coefficient value -.207 and P value 0.230 this indicates that natural learning process is insignificant on fraud detection. Huge investment in acquisition of deep learning machine should be ensured in order to boost fraud detection and protection in credit issuing and assessment in order to improve corporate performance of banks.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing: Rethinking Strategic Practices and Consumer Engagement
all.venue: Recent Trends in Data Mining and Business Forecasting
all.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a routine part of digital marketing, helping firms analyse behavioural data, personalise communication, automate customer service and forecast demand, yet evidence on its benefits and limits remains scattered. This paper is a narrative review based entirely on secondary research. Peer-reviewed articles, academic books, statutes and judicial decisions were identified through structured searches of four databases, screened against stated inclusion criteria, appraised for relevance and quality, and grouped into five themes through thematic analysis. Seven applications are reviewed, namely personalised advertising, social media marketing, chatbots, content creation, predictive analytics, customer relationship management, and email marketing with search engine optimisation. The synthesis shows that efficiency gains are reported most consistently, whereas the effects of personalisation on customer engagement and purchase intention are conditional on transparency, perceived control and consumer trust. Studies differ mainly in context, disclosure, and trust, and few examine Indian consumers. On this basis, the paper proposes a conceptual framework linking AI-driven personalisation, privacy concern, consumer trust, customer engagement and purchase intention, expressed as seven propositions for future testing and not as established.

all.title: Adoption of Artificial Intelligence Tools Among Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Pune: Opportunities, Challenges, and Business Impact
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Many Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Pune are gradually exploring Artificial Intelligence (AI) to manage routine work, understand customers better, and make faster business decisions. Although AI can offer clear advantages, many smaller firms hesitate to adopt it because of limited funds, shortage of trained staff, weak digital systems, and uncertainty about returns. This paper reviews recent literature on AI adoption in SMEs, with a focus on Pune and the wider Indian MSME environment. It examines how tools such as chatbots, generative AI, automation software, predictive analytics, and AI-enabled customer relationship management systems are being used in areas such as marketing, sales, customer service, finance, and operations. The review finds that AI can improve productivity, customer engagement, decision-making, and competitiveness when it is introduced gradually and matched to actual business needs. At the same time, cost, lack of awareness, poor data quality, integration problems, privacy concerns, and employee resistance continue to restrict adoption. The study suggests that Pune SMEs are more likely to benefit from affordable, cloud-based AI tools, practical training, strong management support, and a phased implementation approach rather than large-scale digital transformation.

all.title: Emerging Horizons of Next-Gen Intelligence
all.abstract: The fast growth of artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) is changing the way modern industrial and service trades work. This chapter describes common uses, including predictive maintenance in manufacturing, generative content in marketing, clinical documentation in health care, and virtual assistants in customer service. Even AI and LLMs have big consequences, the chapter points out some important gaps, such as model hallucinations, lack of interpretability, and partial use in areas with few resources. The main point of this chapter is to find the technological drivers that will define the next generation of AI and LLM systems. The piece also gives a thorough look at new trends that are worth initial consideration, like superior contextual understanding, the beginning of autonomous agents and AI co-pilots, domain-specific and low-resource LLMs, acceptable AI design, and full-scale multimodal mixing.

all.title: Institutional responsibility for harm caused by algorithmic systems
institutions: Southwest University of Political Science & Law
all.abstract: When an automated system is implicated in harm, the institution that deployed it sometimes claims, at the moment of accountability, that the system was the author of the outcome. In February 2024, a tribunal in British Columbia described an airline’s defence in exactly these terms, as a submission that its customer-service chatbot was ‘a separate legal entity that is responsible for its own actions’, and rejected it. This article has two objectives. The first is to specify and evidence this move, termed here attributional displacement. Drawing on twelve episodes resolved between 2016 and 2025, each documented in an official record that captures both the attribution and its resolution, the article shows that the move belongs to the defensive pleadings and statements of institutions facing liability, and not to critical scholarship on artificial intelligence, which has named firms and executives from the outset. The second objective is to explain when the move succeeds. Three conditions are identified: an evidentiary presumption that the system operated correctly, a human operator at the point of harm who can be blamed in its place, and an affected group with little capacity to contest the attribution. Where all three hold, displacement can survive for years, as it did for sixteen years in the Post Office Horizon prosecutions in England and Wales. Where any one is absent, it tends to fail quickly: the airline’s argument, which enjoyed no presumption, had no operator to blame and faced a claimant with cheap access to the tribunal, was rejected in a single paragraph. To account for this pattern, the article integrates five established concepts into a single sequence, which it terms the techno-scapegoat cycle, and shows that the cycle’s final stage, at which accountability disappears, is constituted by rules of evidence and procedure rather than by organisational habit alone.

all.title: SecureNEET: A Blockchain-Enabled, AI-Powered Examination Management and Learning Platform
all.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
authors: Angel Mariya P J, Anupama M V, Devika M A
Fathima Shabnas U T, Sibi Sasidharan, Anjitha P
all.abstract: Question paper leakage threatens the credibility of national-level examinations such as the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET). Conventional systems rely on centralized storage and manual distribution of papers, exposing them to insider threats, cyberattacks and early access, while students depend on several disconnected platforms for preparation. This paper presents SecureNEET, a blockchain-enabled, AI-powered examination management and learning platform with an Admin web application, an Exam Center web application and a Student Flutter mobile application sharing a Django backend and a MySQL database. Random NEET-format papers are generated from a Question Bank populated with Admin-approved, AI-generated questions. Each paper is protected with SHA-256 hashing and AES-256-CBC encryption, bound to an auto-decrypt time, and its hash and a unique QR token are recorded on an Ethereum blockchain through a Solidity smart contract. An Exam Center can download a paper only after the release time and after QR and 6-digit email OTP verification, and every attempt is logged for the Admin. Students are verified using face recognition with 128-dimensional dlib ResNet embeddings and ID proof, and login activity is monitored by rule-based anomaly detection. The Student application provides a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot, AI quick-revision summaries, AI mock tests and previous-year papers. SecureNEET thus combines secure examination management with continuous student preparation in a single platform

all.title: Automate the Back, Humanize the Front: Hybrid Intelligence and the Strategic Value of Human Frontline Service under AI Commoditization
all.venue: Journal of Enterprise Strategy and Management Innovation
institutions: First Asia Institute of Technology and Humanities
all.abstract: Firms across service industries are replacing customer-facing employees with chatbots, voice agents, and other AI systems, usually on the grounds of labour savings and throughput. This paper examines whether, and under what conditions, human frontline interaction remains a source of competitive value as AI service capabilities spread. Using a conceptual design built on an integrative literature review, it synthesises five bodies of research that have developed largely separately: frontline service automation, algorithm aversion, relationship marketing and the resource-based view, the digital exclusion of vulnerable consumers, and human–AI collaboration. The synthesis indicates that automation does not generally improve customer outcomes. Automated agents perform reliably in routine, structured encounters but fall short where tasks are ambiguous, emotionally charged, or consequential. Customers tend to judge algorithmic errors harshly, hold the deploying firm responsible for them, and generalise failures across automated systems. A resource-based reading suggests that as AI service capabilities become widely accessible and are perceived as interchangeable, they tend toward competitive parity. Human frontline service, by contrast, may meet the conditions of a strategic resource where firms invest in it as a capability. The paper develops a front-stage/back-stage hybrid intelligence framework that classifies service touchpoints by task ambiguity, consequence stakes, emotional intensity, and customer vulnerability, and it advances seven propositions for empirical testing. Implications are drawn for Southeast Asian service economies, including the Philippine IT-BPM sector and ASEAN retail banking, without treating the region as homogeneous. The analysis is conceptual and does not establish causal effects on firm performance. For practitioners, it offers a structured basis for deciding where automation belongs and where human capability should remain at the point of customer contact.

all.title: Pengembangan Platform Marketplace Jasa Pengecatan Kendaraan Berbasis Web Dengan Pengujian Fungsional dan Validasi Ahli
all.abstract: Vehicle painting services are still largely managed conventionally, which makes it hard for customers to compare workshops, obtain cost estimates, and monitor work progress, while workshops lack an integrated digital channel. This study aims to design and build ZaCoating App, a web-based vehicle painting service marketplace, and to test how well its functions meet the functional requirements. The study follows a Software Engineering Research approach with the Waterfall model. The system is built with Laravel 12, PHP 8.3, and MySQL, with role-based access control for four user roles (user, partner workshop, customer service, and operator). Its main features are a five-step ordering wizard, price quotations, a ten-stage progress tracker, staged payment through Midtrans (30% down payment and 70% final payment, sandbox mode), and a virtual assistant with automatic fallback among Gemini, Groq, and Ollama, keyword-based product retrieval (RAG), and vehicle photo analysis. Testing combined automated testing and black-box testing on 18 scenarios that cover 29 functional requirements, followed by validation from two lecturers and a developer self-evaluation, both using an 18-statement five-point Likert instrument. All 18 scenarios passed (100%). Expert validation produced a score of 87.22% with a "feasible" conclusion from both validators, while the self-evaluation produced 92.22% and is used only for comparison because it is not independent. These results indicate that the system works as specified in the test environment. Security, performance, end-user usability, and the quality of the artificial intelligence features have not been tested, so production readiness requires further testing.

all.title: Top Claude Partners 2026
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Implementing Claude in a business environment involves much more than connecting an API to an existing application. Organizations need to consider how AI will access internal data, interact with business systems, support everyday workflows, and operate securely over time. This is why selecting experienced Claude implementation partners is an important decision for companies planning to move beyond AI experiments. The right development team can help organizations turn promising prototypes into reliable, maintainable solutions that deliver practical business value. However, not every technology provider offers the same level of expertise. Some teams specialize in simple chatbot development, while others focus on complex integrations, enterprise architecture, automation, and AI-powered business applications. Understanding these differences makes it easier to identify the right implementation approach. Why businesses need experienced Claude implementation partners Claude can support various business processes, including document analysis, customer service, knowledge management, research assistance, and internal workflow automation. However, successful implementation depends on more than the capabilities of the AI model itself. Companies must determine which processes would benefit from AI, what information the system needs to access, and how employees will interact with the technology. Experienced Claude implementation partners can help businesses evaluate these requirements before development begins. An implementation partner should also understand how AI applications connect with existing software infrastructure. This may include customer relationship management platforms, enterprise resource planning systems, internal databases, and custom business applications. Without careful planning, organizations risk creating isolated AI tools that provide limited operational value. Essential Claude AI implementation services Professional Claude AI implementation services cover several important stages of enterprise AI adoption. The process usually begins with a discovery phase, during which the development team evaluates business requirements, technical limitations, available data, and possible AI use cases. Once the project scope is established, the provider can design an integration architecture that supports the organization's specific needs. Typical implementation services may include: — Claude API integration with existing applications.— Development of AI-powered assistants and workflow automation.— Integration with internal databases and knowledge management systems.— Implementation of authentication and access permissions.— Monitoring, testing, and performance optimization.— Ongoing maintenance and improvements after deployment. The objective is not simply to make the AI model generate useful responses. It is to create a system that employees can use consistently within established business processes. Technical expertise The provider should demonstrate practical knowledge of LLM integration, API development, backend architecture, cloud infrastructure, and data processing. Experience with retrieval-augmented generation, structured outputs, and AI workflow automation can also be valuable for more complex projects. Relevant project experience Companies should examine whether the development team has worked with similar business requirements or technical environments. A provider experienced in internal knowledge assistants may approach a project differently from one specializing in automated financial document processing. Security and data management AI applications may interact with confidential business information, customer records, or proprietary internal documents. Implementation teams should be able to explain how they handle permissions, sensitive information, access control, and data protection. Long-term support Launching an AI application is only one stage of the development process. Organizations should understand how the provider handles updates, system monitoring, troubleshooting, and future improvements. A reliable partner should offer a clear plan for maintaining the solution after deployment. Understanding enterprise Claude integration Enterprise Claude integration introduces challenges that may not appear in smaller experimental projects. Large organizations often operate multiple software platforms, maintain complex permission structures, and follow established information security policies. Connecting AI technology with these environments requires a carefully designed architecture. For example, an AI-powered internal assistant may need to retrieve information from several business systems while ensuring that employees only access information they are authorized to view. The development team must also consider how the system handles incomplete information, unexpected responses, and integration failures. A production-ready solution should include appropriate monitoring, error handling, and human oversight where necessary. These measures help organizations reduce operational risks while making AI functionality more dependable. The implementation should include appropriate review processes and safeguards for sensitive customer information. These workflows may be useful in industries such as finance, legal services, logistics, and professional consulting. Business workflow automation Claude can also become part of broader automation systems that process incoming information, assist with routine decisions, or prepare structured outputs for other applications. Each use case should be evaluated against measurable business objectives rather than implemented simply because the technology is available. Choosing an implementation partner in Eastern Europe Eastern Europe is one region businesses may consider when searching for external software development and AI integration teams. The region includes technology companies offering custom software development, enterprise system integration, cloud engineering, and AI-related services. However, location alone should not determine the choice of provider. Organizations should evaluate the team's technical qualifications, communication practices, project management approach, and experience working with international clients. It is also important to discuss delivery expectations, collaboration tools, documentation standards, and the availability of ongoing technical support. Comparing these factors helps businesses identify providers that align with their operational requirements and preferred collaboration model. For example, businesses may ask how the team evaluates potential AI use cases, what architecture it recommends, and which security controls will be included. They should also discuss project milestones, testing procedures, performance monitoring, and post-launch responsibilities. An experienced provider should be able to explain both the benefits and limitations of the proposed solution. all.title: ALTERNATIVE DIGITAL FINANCE IN THE GLOBAL FINANCIAL MARKET SYSTEM: CURRENT TRENDS AND STRUCTURAL TRANSFORMATIONS
all.venue: Scientific Notes of Taurida National V I Vernadsky University Series Economy and Management
institutions: State University of Trade and Economics
all.abstract: The article examines current trends and structural transformations in alternative digital finance within the global financial market. It systematises changes in market geography, business models, funding sources, data and technology use, regulatory approaches, and systemic integration. The study identifies a shift from predominantly P2P models towards hybrid forms combining digital platforms, banks, institutional investors, and technology companies. It highlights the growing role of the United States and the Americas following the contraction of China’s P2P segment, as well as the increasing importance of institutional funding, embedded finance, and automated credit assessment. It is argued that the sector’s development reflects not the displacement of traditional intermediaries, but the platform-based reintermediation of financial relations.

all.title: FinTech-Enabled Mobile Banking Services and Bank Performance: An Empirical Analysis of HDFC Bank
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: FinTech-Enabled Mobile Banking Services and Bank Performance: An Empirical Analysis of HDFC Bank Dr. Spoorthi Patil Associate Professor, Sharnbasva University, Kalaburagi, Karnataka, India Abstract: Indian banking is one of the largest banking systems in the world. It caters the diverse needs of customers. Fintech, the application of digital technology to financial services, is reshaping the future of finance so this study examines the impact of fintech mobile banking services on HDFC Bank's performance. Secondary data have been chosen for the study and financial data is collected form HDFC and RBI website for 12 years. Correlation is used for statistical analysis using SPSS Software. Analysis of key financial metrics reveals significant growth in equity, assets, income, and profits, indicating successful digital transformation. Findings show varying correlations between transaction volumes/values and financial ratios. Higher transaction values correlate with improved net margins and reduced financial costs, while increased volumes and values negatively impact Return on Equity (ROE). Return on Assets (ROA) shows consistent efficiency. Keywords: Banking, FinTech, Mobile Banking, Banking Services, HDFC Bank, Bank Performance

all.title: Digital Transformation and Organisational Performance in a Nigerian Tier-One Bank: Evidence from Access Bank Plc, 2019 to 2025
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between digital transformation and organisational performance in Access Bank Plc, the Nigerian commercial bank with the largest customer franchise, utilizing audited financial disclosures spanning 2019 to 2025. Employing an ex post facto case research design with the bank-year as the unit of analysis, digital transformation is operationalised through three verifiable metrics: channels and other e-business income (a fee-based accounting line excluding digital lending interest), IT and e-business expenditure, and disclosed digital architecture initiatives. Organisational performance is measured via gross revenue, profit before tax (PBT), profit after tax (PAT), PBT margin, and end-of-year return on assets (ROA). Data are consistently drawn from the consolidated banking group statements across the 2022 corporate reorganisation establishing Access Holdings Plc as ultimate parent. Between 2019 and 2025, channels and other e-business income expanded from ₦36.041 billion to ₦206.235 billion, while IT and e-business expenditure increased from ₦9.772 billion to ₦157.888 billion. Over the identical timeframe, gross revenue escalated from ₦666.754 billion to ₦5.385 trillion, PBT grew from ₦115.379 billion to ₦954.248 billion, and total assets expanded from ₦7.147 trillion to ₦51 .267 trillion. Non-parametric Spearman rank correlations reveal strong positive rank concordance between absolute e-business earnings and both gross revenue (ρ = 0.964, p < 0.001) and PBT (ρ = 1 .000, p < 0.001). However, digital revenue intensity contracted from a peak of 7.33% in 2020 to 3.83% in 2025, attributable to a denomination effect wherein nominal gross earnings were heavily amplified by currency revaluation and high inflation. The evidence demonstrates that digital transformation in Nigerian banking functions primarily as a scale-enabling capability expanding customer reach, transaction velocity, and fee volumes, rather than an automatic short-term profitability driver.

all.title: The Impact of Financing Growth and Digital Transformation on the Financial Performance of Islamic Banks, with Maqasid Sharia as a Moderating Variable
all.venue: Journal of Economic and Business Advancement
all.abstract: This study examines the effects of financing growth and digital transformation on the financial performance of Islamic commercial banks in Indonesia, considering Maqasid Shariah as a moderating variable. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, the analysis draws on secondary data from bank annual reports and official publications covering 2021–2025. Financial performance is measured by return on assets (ROA), financing growth by annual changes in total financing, digital transformation by a six-indicator disclosure index, and Sharia-oriented performance by the Maqasid Sharia Index (MSI). Panel-data regression with interaction terms was estimated using EViews, with specification tests favoring fixed effects. Financing growth (β = 0.003096; p = 0.0001) and digital transformation (β = 0.056793; p = 0.0216) exhibit positive, statistically significant associations with ROA. MSI positively moderates the financing growth relationship (β = 0.001664; p = 0.0014) but negatively moderates the digital transformation relationship (β = −0.008039; p = 0.0439). The reported adjusted R-squared is 0.733720. These findings suggest distinct conditional relationships between Sharia-oriented performance and banking activities rather than uniform profitability effects. However, inconsistencies in the reported MSI descriptive statistics and model output require verification before definitive interpretation. The results support integrated evaluation of profitability, financing expansion, responsible technological development, and Sharia objectives.

all.title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF COMMERCIAL BANKS IN UZBEKISTAN: CURRENT STATE, CHALLENGES AND DEVELOPMENT PROSPECTS
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: This thesis examines the current state, structural challenges, and strategic development prospects of the digital transformation of commercial banks in Uzbekistan. Based on an analysis of Presidential Decrees No. DP-5992 and No. DP-6079, the Central Bank of Uzbekistan’s National Strategy for the Development of Financial Technologies for 2026–2030, Basel Committee digitalization guidelines, and scholarly literature, it is shown that rapid expansion of mobile banking has outpaced core-system modernization and open-API integration. A conditional transformation sequence, an integrated digital architecture principle, and five digital maturity indicators are substantiated.

all.title: Examining the impact of digital transformation on bank profitability: Evidence of lagged and nonlinear effects in Vietnam
all.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractDigital transformation is emerging as a key driver reshaping banking operational models. Empirical evidence on the impact of digital transformation on the profitability of commercial banks remains inconclusive, particularly in the context of emerging economies like Vietnam. This study aims to assess the impact of digital transformation on the profitability of Vietnamese commercial banks, while also examining lagged effects, non-linear relationships, and the role of income diversification. The research is grounded in a theoretical framework combining the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory. This study uses panel data from 16 Vietnamese commercial banks from 2010-2024, totaling 240 observations. The main methodology employed is a two-way fixed-effects model combined with standard errors and robustness testing using Driscoll–Kraay standard errors combined with an alternative specification to check the robustness of the results. Empirical results show that digital transformation has a positive impact on bank profitability, and this impact appears non-linear. Meanwhile, the study has not found empirical evidence of a one-period lagged impact of digital transformation and the moderating role of income diversification. These findings imply that, to effectively leverage digital transformation strategies, banks need not only to invest comprehensively in technology, resources, and data, but also to enhance their capacity to exploit and utilize digital resources and develop a digital ecosystem. The research findings contribute to the empirical evidence regarding the impact of digital transformation on profitability in the banking sector of emerging economies.

all.title: Digital finance and bank ESG performance: A non-linear analysis of Chinese listed banks
all.abstract: In response to China’s dual-carbon goals and the rapid development of digital technologies, increasing attention has been devoted to the role of digital finance in sustainable banking. However, its potential nonlinear effects on bank ESG performance remain underexplored. Using an unbalanced panel of 42 Chinese listed commercial banks from 2012 to 2024, this study examines the impact of digital finance on bank ESG performance through a two-way fixed effects model. The results reveal a significant U-shaped relationship: digital finance is negatively associated with ESG performance at lower levels of development, whereas the estimated association turns positive beyond the turning point. Mechanism analysis suggests that green innovation serves as a potential transmission channel. Further analysis indicates that digital transformation and bank operating efficiency strengthen this association, whereas financial regulation weakens it, a pattern consistent with an institutional substitution explanation. The nonlinear association also varies across bank and regional characteristics. These findings remain broadly stable across multiple robustness and endogeneity tests. This study enriches the literature on digital finance and sustainable banking by highlighting the stage-dependent nature of digital finance and providing implications for threshold-informed digital finance governance and differentiated ESG strategies for Chinese listed commercial banks.

all.title: Digital Transformation in Banking and Employee Knowledge of Digital Technologies
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: What a bank gets back from its technology spending depends less on the systems it buys than on whether the people using them understand what they are for. This paper builds a theoretical framework around three constructs: digital transformation in banking, the level of employee knowledge of the technologies that drive it, and the demographic attributes that shape how that knowledge is distributed. It draws on the digital transformation literature, on technology acceptance research, and on human capital and absorptive capacity theory, treating these as complementary accounts of how knowledge becomes organisational performance. Transformation is specified as a strategic and cultural reorganisation rather than the digitisation of existing procedures, a distinction used here to separate genuine change from cosmetic modernisation. Employee knowledge is then broken into four dimensions: technical understanding, awareness of banking applications, practical skill in use, and awareness of risk and regulatory obligation, on the grounds that a single composite score conceals more than it reveals about where a workforce stands. The paper reviews what is known about age, gender, education, experience and job title as correlates of that knowledge, arguing each is better read as a proxy for exposure and prior learning than as a fixed capacity. It closes with five propositions that a cross-sectional survey could test, covering the dimensionality of the knowledge construct, its association with perceived job performance, its demographic correlates, and the moderating role of organisational support. The framework is intended to support instrument design and the targeting of training budgets in commercial banks, so that scarce resources are directed at diagnosed gaps rather than distributed evenly.

all.title: The Role of Digital Transformation in Reducing Operational Risks: A Survey Study in a Sample of Private Banks in Erbil Governorate.
all.venue: Polytechnic Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences
all.abstract: This research aims to examine the role of digital transformation dimensions in mitigating operational risks within a sample of private banks operating in Erbil Governorate. The study employed a descriptive-analytical approach using a cross-sectional survey methodology. Eighty (80) questionnaires, each consisting of 30 items distributed across three axes according to a five-point Likert scale, were distributed. Sixty-seven (67) questionnaires were returned and deemed valid for statistical analysis using SPSS v27. The study reached several conclusions, most notably a statistically significant positive relationship between digital transformation and operational risk reduction. The Pearson correlation coefficient between the digital transformation variable as a whole and operational risk reduction was approximately ($r = 0.722) with a significance level ($p < 0.001), indicating a strong and statistically significant correlation between the two variables. In light of the findings, the study recommended that private banks fully integrate digital transformation strategies with operational risk mitigation management frameworks so that digital transformation projects are not implemented as isolated technological initiatives or mere technology investments but are accompanied by the systematic and comprehensive identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of operational risks, and ensuring their compatibility with internal control procedures and business continuity.

all.title: THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF FINANCIAL AND BANKING SERVICES IN IRAQ (2010-2023)
all.abstract: The objective of this study was to quantify and analyze the effects of digital transformation in all its aspects (Technology infrastructure, Electronic payment systems, Financial technology tools and Salary domiciliation project) on financial/banking services development and financial inclusion in the Iraqi banking sector from 2010 to 2023. This was done using a descriptive-analytical approach and econometric time-series analysis, where the influence and statistical significance of the relationships between the variables studied were evaluated through regression models. The analysis was done on official data of Central Bank of Iraq and statistical bulletins released by the Central Statistical Organization in Iraq. The results showed that the impact of digital transformation on improving the efficiency and quality of banking services and financial inclusion in Iraq is statistically significant (Sig. F = 0.000). The model adopted was able to explain 91.4% of the variations observed (R² = 0.914). The analysis showed that the most influential factor that stimulates banking transactions was the salary domiciliation project (regression coefficient β = 0.412) followed by the infrastructure development such as the POS terminal and ATM (β = 0.384) and then by the electronic retail payment systems (IRPSI) (β = 0.296). The results also show that there has been a change in the philosophy of banking service delivery in Iraq that has moved from the "physical bank branches" to "direct digital channels." The total amount of beneficiaries disbursing salaries via the banking system has increased to 9.3 million employees/retirees, with an increase in the number of Point-of-Sale (POS) terminals to 71.0 per 100,000 adults. At the same time, the share of cash outside the banking system has dropped from 84.7% in 2015 to 66.3% in 2023 and the financial inclusion index of the adult population has increased to 48.5%. Based on the results, the study makes a number of recommendations, including: reforming legislation and laws on digital financial transactions and electronic identity; opening a regulatory sandbox for fintech; creating tax and procedural stimulus for enterprises to require full cash payment ("cash-out") to use POS terminals; and implementing national financial education strategies to reduce the use of cash in transactions and move toward a cashless society.

all.title: The Impact of Intellectual Capital, Digital Transformation Capability, and Innovation Culture on Organizational Performance: The Role of Competitive Intensity as a Resource Value Reallocation Mechanism in Vietnamese Commercial Banks
all.venue: International Journal of Analysis and Applications
institutions: Ho Chi Minh University of Banking
all.abstract: The pressure on commercial banks has increased due to digitalization, fintech development, and changing customer demands. This study examines the effects of intellectual capital, digital transformation capability, and innovation culture on organizational performance, while investigating the moderating role of competitive intensity in Vietnamese commercial banks. Drawing on the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities view, and contingency theory, the study develops and tests a research model using survey data collected from 551 managerial staff members of Vietnamese commercial banks. The results reveal that intellectual capital, digital transformation capability, and innovation culture positively affect organizational performance, with innovation culture showing the strongest effect. Competitive intensity has a negative direct effect on organizational performance and produces asymmetric moderating effects by weakening the contribution of intellectual capital while strengthening the effects of digital transformation capability and innovation culture. The findings highlight that the value of strategic resources depends on competitive conditions and suggest that banks should prioritize adaptive capabilities, particularly digital transformation and innovation culture, to improve organizational performance.

all.title: Digital Transformation Pathways for the Banking Sector in the Hainan Free Trade Port
all.venue: European Journal of Business Economics & Management
institutions: Hainan Vocational University of Science and Technology
all.abstract: The establishment and continued development of the Hainan Free Trade Port are part of China's efforts to deepen domestic reform and open its economy further. Hainan's place in national strategy reflects its role as a link in the Maritime Silk Road and a gateway to the New International Land–Sea Trade Corridor. Financial services support the province's other industries and influence how it uses its natural resources. Digital transformation can help financial institutions compete by developing new services and, in Hainan, change how they meet the needs of the real economy. This study examines how far digital transformation has progressed among financial institutions in the port, what has slowed implementation, and how digital services are likely to develop. The analysis provides a conceptual basis and practical guidance for developing the port's financial sector, including policy recommendations to speed up implementation.

all.title: The mediating role of digital transformation in the relationship between social media marketing, mobile marketing, and marketing performance: Evidence from the Jordanian banking sector
all.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study investigates the mediating role of digital transformation (DT) in the relationships between social media marketing (SMM), mobile marketing (MBM), and marketing performance (MP) in the Jordanian banking sector. Data were collected from 272 bank branch managers representing banking institutions across Jordan between May and November 2024. The study employed Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS 4 to test the proposed relationships. Internal consistency and convergent validity were confirmed through Cronbach’s Alpha values ranging from 0.820 to 0.903, composite reliability values ranging from 0.873 to 0.923, and Average Variance Extracted (AVE) values ranging from 0.579 to 0.650. The structural model explained 27.5% of the variance in digital transformation (R² = 0.275) and 59.9% of the variance in marketing performance (R² = 0.599). The findings revealed that mobile marketing has a significant positive effect on marketing performance (β = 0.155, p = 0.001), whereas social media marketing does not have a significant direct effect on marketing performance (β = 0.093, p = 0.058). Both social media marketing and mobile marketing significantly influence digital transformation (β = 0.315, p < 0.001; β = 0.320, p < 0.001), while digital transformation exerts a strong positive effect on marketing performance (β = 0.646, p < 0.001). Furthermore, digital transformation fully mediates the relationship between social media marketing and marketing performance (β = 0.203, p < 0.001) and partially mediates the relationship between mobile marketing and marketing performance (β = 0.206, p < 0.001). The findings highlight the critical role of digital transformation in converting digital marketing capabilities into improved marketing performance and provide practical insights for banking institutions seeking to enhance competitiveness in an increasingly digital environment.AcknowledgmentsThis research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

all.title: EMERGING MARKET FINANCE IN A FRAGMENTING GLOBAL ECONOMY: BANKING RESILIENCE, DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION, AND INVESTMENT REALIGNMENT (2024–2026)
all.venue: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
all.abstract: The global economic landscape in the mid-2020s is undergoing profound structural change, marked by geopolitical fragmentation, deglobalization, and rapid digital transformation.Within this context, emerging markets have transitioned from being peripheral participants to central anchors of global economic resilience.This study examines the evolving financial and investment ecosystems of key emerging regions-India, Brazil, and Southeast Asia-during the 2024-2026 period.Using a mixed-methods synthesis of secondary data from international financial institutions, central banks, and investment reports, the research evaluates banking sector stability, foreign direct investment (FDI) dynamics, and the disruptive role of fintech and artificial intelligence.The findings reveal that strengthened monetary frameworks, improved asset quality, and institutional credibility have enhanced emerging market resilience to global shocks.Simultaneously, supply-chain realignment under the "China Plus One" strategy has redirected capital flows toward ASEAN and India, while Brazil illustrates how digital finance can coexist with high interest rates.However, rising unsecured retail credit, fiscal vulnerabilities, and regulatory fragmentation present new systemic risks.The study concludes that sustainable growth in emerging markets will depend on balancing digital financial innovation with prudent regulation and maintaining strong domestic financial institutions to attract long-term investment in a fragmented global economy.

all.title: Impact of Financial Efficiency on Profitability of Deposit Money Banks
all.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
all.abstract: The profitability of deposit money banks remained fundamental to financial system stability, efficient financial intermediation, and sustainable economic growth. However, the persistent fluctuations in the profitability of Nigerian deposit money banks despite several successive reforms, recapitalisation programmes, prudential regulations and other measures introduced to strengthen the Nigerian banking system. This paper therefore examined the impact of financial efficiency on the profitability of deposit money banks in Nigeria over the period 2005Q1–2025Q4. Specifically, the paper investigated the effects of bank overhead costs to total assets, bank net interest margin, and bank cost-to-income ratio on bank profitability measured by return on assets (ROA). The paper adopted an ex-post facto research design and utilized the Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS) estimation technique. The results showed that bank overhead costs to total assets exerted a negative but statistically insignificant impact on return on assets. This implied that although increases in operating and administrative expenses relative to total assets tended to reduce the profitability of deposit money banks, the impact was not sufficiently strong to significantly influence profitability during the paper period. Bank net interest margin had a positive and statistically significant impact on profitability. This indicated that improvements in banks' ability to generate net interest income from their earning assets significantly enhanced return on assets, highlighting the importance of efficient intermediation in sustaining bank profitability. The bank cost-to-income ratio exerted a negative and statistically significant impact on return on assets. The finding suggested that increases in operating expenses relative to operating income significantly weakened the profitability of deposit money banks, emphasizing the need for prudent cost management and improved operational efficiency to sustain long-run financial performance. Therefore, the paper recommended that the management of deposit money banks should strengthen asset-liability management to sustain higher net interest margins, implement comprehensive cost-management and digital transformation strategies to reduce operating expenses relative to income, while the Central Bank of Nigeria should reinforce supervisory measures that promote operational efficiency and prudent cost management across the banking industry.

all.title: Pengaruh Pengungkapan Environment, Social, dan Governance (ESG) terhadap Bank Performance dengan Transformasi Digital sebagai Variabel Moderasi
all.abstract: This study examines the effect of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure on bank performance, proxied by the natural logarithm of Z-Score, and tests digital transformation as a moderating variable. The study uses a quantitative approach with a sample of 17 banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2022–2024, resulting in 51 firm-year observations. ESG disclosure is measured through content analysis based on the GRI Standards 2021, while digital transformation is measured using keyword-based text mining of annual reports. The data are analyzed using panel data regression and moderated regression analysis with a Common Effect Model and White Diagonal robust standard errors to address heteroskedasticity. The results show that Environmental, Social, and Governance disclosure do not have statistically significant direct effects on bank performance.
